  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.

  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }

    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");

  }

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Desingularizations of Conformally
<br class="ltx_break">Kähler, Einstein Orbifolds</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">
<span id="id1" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle" style="width:126.5pt;">
<span id="id1.1" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center">Claude LeBrun</span>
<span id="id1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="id1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Stony Brook University</span></span>
</span>
</span><span id="id2" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_funding ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span>Supported in part by NSF grant DMS-2203572.</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before">  </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">and   
<span id="id3" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_parbox ltx_align_middle" style="width:108.4pt;">

<span id="id3.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="id3.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">MIT</span></span>

</span><span id="id4" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_funding ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span>Supported in part by NSF grant
DMS-2405328.</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{(M,g_{i})\}_{i=1}^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{(M,g_{i})\}_{i=1}^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> be a sequence of smooth compact oriented Einstein <math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds of
fixed Einstein constant <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> that
Gromov-Hausdorff converges
to a <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Einstein orbifold <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>. Suppose, moreover, that
the limit metric <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> is <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hermitian</span> with respect to some complex structure on the limit orbifold <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>,
that <math id="abstract1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> has at least one singular point, and that every gravitational instanton
that bubbles off from <math id="abstract1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is <span id="abstract1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">anti-self-dual</span>. Then, for all sufficiently large <math id="abstract1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
the given <math id="abstract1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are all Kähler-Einstein. As a consequence, the limit orbifold <math id="abstract1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is also
Kähler-Einstein, and must in fact be one of the orbifold limits classified <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite> by Odaka, Spotti, and Sun.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Three decades ago, Anderson <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>]</cite> and Bando-Kasue-Nakajima <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite> discovered a generalization of Gromov’s compactness theorem <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>]</cite> that gives
<math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Einstein <span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">orbifolds</span> a previously-unsuspected central role
in the theory of smooth compact Einstein <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds.
For example, if we are given a sequence <math id="S1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{i},g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{i},g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> of smooth compact connected Einstein <math id="S1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds of fixed Einstein constant <math id="S1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>
and fixed Euler characteristic, with volumes <math id="S1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\vol(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Vol</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\vol(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly bounded
away from zero, then there exists a subsequence <math id="S1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M_{i_{j}},g_{i_{j}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M_{i_{j}},g_{i_{j}})</annotation></semantics></math> that converges in the
Gromov-Hausdorff distance
to a compact connected <math id="S1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Einstein orbifold <math id="S1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> with the same Einstein constant <math id="S1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>.
After further refining our subsequence, we may moreover arrange <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> that the manifolds <math id="S1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{i_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><msub><mi>i</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{i_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math> are all diffeomorphic<span id="footnote1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnote"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">1</sup>
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_note">1</span>
            
            
          The
phenomenon of diffeomorphism-finiteness that is operative here
has more recently been shown <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, Theorem 1.12]</cite> to hold under dramatically weaker hypotheses.</span></span></span> to
some reference smooth compact <math id="S1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold <math id="S1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
The singularities of the limit orbifold <math id="S1.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> are moreover isolated, and so
constitute a finite subset <math id="S1.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{S}\subset X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔖</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{S}\subset X</annotation></semantics></math>, while their complement <math id="S1.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X-\mathfrak{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝔖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X-\mathfrak{S}</annotation></semantics></math> is diffeomorphic to a connected
open set <math id="S1.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U\subset M</annotation></semantics></math>. Furthermore, after moving the metrics in the sequence by a suitable sequence of self-diffeomorphisms of <math id="S1.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>,
the weak-limit
metric <math id="S1.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S1.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X-\mathfrak{S}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝔖</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X-\mathfrak{S}</annotation></semantics></math> actually becomes the <math id="S1.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>C</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> limit on compact subsets of the given sequence of Einstein metrics restricted to <math id="S1.p1.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U\subset M</annotation></semantics></math>. Meanwhile,
the Riemannian diameter of each connected component of <math id="S1.p1.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M-U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M-U</annotation></semantics></math> shrinks to zero, but the <math id="S1.p1.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> norm of the curvature
on each such component remains bounded away from zero.
After suitably scaling up these high-curvature regions,
their pointed Gromov-Hausdorff limits then yield Ricci-flat ALE spaces that are said to <span id="S1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">bubble off</span> from <math id="S1.p1.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. One subtlety
is that curvature can accumulate at different length scales, so that some of these ALE limits could themselves be orbifolds. However,
any orbifold singularity of such an ALE space in turn arises from a <span id="S1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">deeper bubble</span>. This hierarchy of scales however terminates in finitely many steps, and the <span id="S1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">deepest bubbles</span>
that thereby arise are therefore smooth. By reversing the process, one can then reconstruct the smooth manifold <math id="S1.p1.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> from <math id="S1.p1.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite> cutting out a neighborhood
of each orbifold singularity, replacing it with a diffeomorphic copy of the corresponding bubble, and then iterating the process until all the orbifold singularities have been removed.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">While the above results indicate that certain Einstein orbifolds can arise as limits of smooth Einstein <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds, the second author’s previous results <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> have definitively shown that not
every Einstein orbifold arises in this way. The
present article focuses on the problem of determining which compact <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional <span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">Kähler-Einstein</span> orbifolds with <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>
can be expressed as limits of sequences of smooth Einstein <math id="S1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds. If one specializes the problem by requiring that all the smooth Einstein manifolds in the limiting sequence
be <span id="S1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">Kähler-Einstein</span> manifolds, then
a complete answer has already been given by Odaka-Spotti-Sun <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>.
But if we now relax our assumptions, and allow the metrics in the given sequence to have arbitrary holonomy, one might still
hope that the
list of possible Kähler-Einstein orbifold limits might remain unaffected. Unfortunately, however, there is a serious technical obstacle to proving such a statement. The root cause of this difficulty is that we currently lack a
complete classification of
Ricci-flat ALE manifolds.
Indeed, all known examples of such ALE manifolds are half-conformally-flat, so that, when correctly oriented, they
satisfy <math id="S1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\in\End_{0}(\Lambda^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>End</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\in\End_{0}(\Lambda^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the self-dual piece of the Weyl curvature tensor. While a longstanding conjecture claims
that all Ricci-flat ALE <math id="S1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds are in fact of this type, the best available result in support of this conjecture <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite> assumes
the existence of a spin structure on the universal cover of the ALE space for which one of the chiral spin bundles has trivial monodromy at infinity;
but, unfortunately,
no one has yet discovered a compelling reason why this assumption
should <span id="S1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a priori</span>
always be valid. In this paper, our approach will skirt this issue entirely via recourse to the following definition:</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 1</span></span><span id="Thmdefn1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M^{4},g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M^{4},g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> be a
sequence of compact oriented <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Einstein manifolds
that converges to a positive-scalar-curvature compact Einstein orbifold <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>
in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense. We will then say that <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> is an </span><span id="Thmdefn1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">admissible sequence</span><span id="Thmdefn1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and that
<math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is an </span><span id="Thmdefn1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">admissible orbifold limit</span><span id="Thmdefn1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,
if every Ricci-flat ALE space <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,\mathsf{h})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝗁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y,\mathsf{h})</annotation></semantics></math> that bubbles off from the <math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>
satisfies
<math id="Thmdefn1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math> with respect to the induced orientation.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">While restricting our attention to admissible sequences will of course narrow the scope of our
investigation, it will nonetheless allow us to prove the following rather satisfying results:</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmmain1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_main">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmmain1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A</span></span><span id="Thmmain1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmmain1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmmain1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmmain1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be a compact Kähler-Einstein orbifold of Einstein constant <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and let
<math id="Thmmain1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M^{4},g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M^{4},g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>
be an admissible sequence of compact oriented Einstein manifolds with <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> as its orbifold limit.
Then, for all <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are actually all Kähler-Einstein.
In particular, <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> must be one of the Kähler-Einstein orbifolds classified by Odaka-Spotti-Sun.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Indeed, essentially the same result will also follow even if one merely assumes that <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> is <span id="S1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hermitian</span>, in the sense that
<math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g_{\infty}(J\cdot,J\cdot)=g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>J</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}(J\cdot,J\cdot)=g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> for some integrable orbifold complex structure <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmmain2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_main">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmmain2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem B</span></span><span id="Thmmain2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmmain2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmmain2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmmain2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be a compact connected
Einstein orbifold of Einstein constant <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and suppose that <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> is Hermitian
with respect to some integrable orbifold complex structure <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="J" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>J</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>.
If <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> has at least one singular point, and if <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is an admissible sequence of Einstein manifolds
converging to <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, then the <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> are Kähler-Einstein for all <math id="Thmmain2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>,
and
<math id="Thmmain2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is one of the Kähler-Einstein orbifold limits classified by Odaka-Spotti-Sun.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Singularities of Type T</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is the orbifold limit of some admissible sequence <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> of Einstein <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds,
we will show, in Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 2.2. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> below, that
its orbifold singularities must all have the following special property:</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2</span></span><span id="Thmdefn2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">An isolated orbifold singularity of an oriented orbifold <math id="Thmdefn2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> will be said to be of </span><span id="Thmdefn2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span><span id="Thmdefn2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
if it has an open neighborhood modeled on <math id="Thmdefn2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for some finite subgroup <math id="Thmdefn2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma&lt;SO(4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma&lt;SO(4)</annotation></semantics></math>
for which <math id="Thmdefn2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is also the tangent-cone-at-infinity of an
oriented </span><span id="Thmdefn2.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">anti-self-dual</span><span id="Thmdefn2.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> Ricci-flat ALE manifold <math id="Thmdefn2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y^{4},\mathsf{h})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi>𝗁</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y^{4},\mathsf{h})</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This definition can now
be restated in a more concrete and effective form, as an immediate consequence of the results
of Şuvaina <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite> and Wright <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.1</span></span><span id="S2.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">An oriented singularity <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is
of </span><span id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span><span id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> iff <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma&lt;SO(4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma&lt;SO(4)</annotation></semantics></math> is conjugate to a subgroup of <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U(2)</annotation></semantics></math> of one of the two
following types:</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S2.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S2.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Finite subgroups </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\subset SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\subset SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. These are classified by the simply-laced Dynkin diagrams,
and their images in </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="SO(3)=SU(2)/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">SO(3)=SU(2)/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> are classical symmetry groups of regular polygons or platonic solids.</span></p>
<table id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<thead class="ltx_thead">
<tr id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_tr">

<th id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><math id="S2.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\subset SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\subset SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math></th>
<th id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_r ltx_border_t"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Classical Figure</span></th></tr>
</thead>

</span>
<span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.2.1.2" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_minipage ltx_align_middle" style="width:28.9pt;"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.pic1" class="ltx_picture" style="width:50.0pt;height:5.0pt;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" version="1.1" width="66.42" height="6.64" overflow="visible"><g transform="translate(0,6.64) scale(1,-1)"><g transform="translate(0,3.46)"><circle fill="#000000" r="0.69" stroke="none" stroke-width="0.4" x="0" y="0"/></g><g transform="translate(0,-0.14)"><g transform="translate(0,11.96) scale(1,-1)"><foreignObject width="9.96" height="9.30" overflow="visible"><Math mode="inline" tex="\ldots" text="ldots" xml:id="S2.I1.i1.p1.pic1.m1">

<td id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_border_r ltx_border_tt"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="position:relative; bottom:-5.1pt;"><img src="2601.19215v2/Pentagon.png" id="S2.I1.i1.p1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:24/25;" width="24" height="25" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"></span></td></tr>
<tr id="S2.I1.i1.p1.2.3" class="ltx_tr">

<div id="S2.I1.i1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each such </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,
the corresponding quotient </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">[</span><a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">]</span></cite><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> the tangent cone at infinity
of a family of ALE hyper-Kähler </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-manifolds, each of which is obtained, up to diffeomorphism, by plumbing together copies
of </span><math id="S2.I1.i1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T^{*}S^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>T</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T^{*}S^{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i1.p2.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> according to the intersection pattern dual to the Dynkin diagram.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S2.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S2.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Cyclic groups </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{\ell m^{2}}&lt;U(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≅</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\cong{\mathbb{Z}}_{\ell m^{2}}&lt;U(2)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, that are generated by</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\zeta&amp;\\
&amp;\zeta^{\ell mn-1}\end{array}\right]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>ζ</mi></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><msup><mi>ζ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\zeta&amp;\\
&amp;\zeta^{\ell mn-1}\end{array}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta=e^{2\pi i/\ell m^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ζ</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta=e^{2\pi i/\ell m^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, with </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n&lt;m" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n&lt;m</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gcd(m,n)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>gcd</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>m</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gcd(m,n)=1</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. Such cyclic subgroups are often indicated </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">[</span><a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">]</span></cite><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">
by the shorthand </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{\ell m^{2}}(1,\ell mn-1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\ell m^{2}}(1,\ell mn-1)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.8" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.
For any such subgroup,
</span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.9" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> is the tangent cone at infinity of a
free </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}_{m}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>m</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}_{m}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.10" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">-quotient of a hyper-Kähler manifold of type </span><math id="S2.I1.i2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\ell m-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\ell m-1}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. Conversely, every non-simply-connected Ricci-flat ALE Kähler surface is </span><cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite"><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">[</span><a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">]</span></cite><span id="S2.I1.i2.p1.2.14" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> one of these.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This of course follows from the classification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>, <a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> of oriented Ricci-flat ALE <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds that are <span id="S2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">anti-self-dual</span>, in the sense that <math id="S2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>. Here, one should especially take note of
Wright’s striking theorem that
any such space is Kähler <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite> with respect to some orientation-compatible complex structure.
This fact dovetails nicely with our question, because any singularity of <span id="S2.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span> is therefore modeled on <math id="S2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for some finite group <math id="S2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\subset U(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\subset U(2)</annotation></semantics></math>
that acts freely on the unit sphere <math id="S2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}\subset\mathbb{C}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}\subset\mathbb{C}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and any isolated singularity of an orbifold Kähler surface
is naturally of this form.
However, notice that our requirement that <math id="S2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> must also be the tangent cone at infinity of an anti-self-dual
Ricci-flat ALE manifold
imposes further, less obvious constraints.
Indeed, in the specific setting where <math id="S2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is an orbifold complex surface, singularities of <span id="S2.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span> exactly coincide
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, Proposition 3.10]</cite> with the ones algebraic geometers have traditionally called singularities of <span id="S2.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">class T</span>.
From an algebro-geometric perspective, the key property of these singularities is that they have
<math id="S2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Q}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℚ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Q}}</annotation></semantics></math>-Gorenstein local smoothings. However, the relevance of this class of singularities to our investigation
instead primarily stems from the following differential-geometric observation:</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.2</span></span><span id="S2.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is an admissible orbifold limit, then <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> has only singularities of </span><span id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span><span id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">The subtlety here is that the ALE spaces that bubble off from a given sequence <math id="S2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> might be orbifolds, rather than
manifolds. However, when one surgically replaces each orbifold singularity of such an ALE space with the corresponding deeper bubble, and then iterates the
process until it terminates, the resulting ALE manifold is then diffeomorphic to a Ricci-flat ALE Kähler manifold <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, Theorem 3]</cite>.
Thus, whenever an admissible orbifold limit has a singularity modeled on <math id="S2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for some
<math id="S2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma&lt;U(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma&lt;U(2)</annotation></semantics></math>, then <math id="S2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> is also the tangent cone at infinity of a <span id="S2.p4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">non-singular</span> Ricci-flat ALE Kähler manifold.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">As an immediate consequence, we therefore have:</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.3</span></span><span id="S2.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Among compact Kähler-Einstein orbifolds <math id="S2.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> that have only isolated singularities,
there are infinitely many topological types that
can never arise as limits of admissible sequences of Einstein <math id="S2.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{FS}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{FS}</annotation></semantics></math> be the Fubini-Study metric on <math id="S2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and, for any prime number <math id="S2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>, consider the finite group of isometries of <math id="S2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="({\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2},g_{FS})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>S</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">({\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2},g_{FS})</annotation></semantics></math>
that is generated by</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left[\begin{array}[]{ccc}1&amp;&amp;\\
&amp;\eta&amp;\\
&amp;&amp;\eta^{-1}\end{array}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mn>1</mn></mtd><mtd></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><mi>η</mi></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd></mtd><mtd><msup><mi>η</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[\begin{array}[]{ccc}1&amp;&amp;\\
&amp;\eta&amp;\\
&amp;&amp;\eta^{-1}\end{array}\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p6.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p6.2.1" class="ltx_text">where <math id="S2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta=e^{2\pi i/p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>η</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta=e^{2\pi i/p}</annotation></semantics></math>. The orbifold <math id="S2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> then has exactly three singular points, namely the images of <math id="S2.p6.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[1:0:0]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1:0:0]</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p6.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[0:1:0]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0:1:0]</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.p6.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[0:0:1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>0</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0:0:1]</annotation></semantics></math>,
and each of these three singular points has a neighborhood modeled on a quotient <math id="S2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math>, where the generator of the given <math id="S2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{Z}}_{p}</annotation></semantics></math> action on <math id="S2.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> takes the form</span></p>
<table id="S2.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\eta&amp;\\
&amp;\eta^{-1}\end{array}\right],\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\eta&amp;\\
&amp;\eta^{2}\end{array}\right]^{-1},\mbox{ or }\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\eta&amp;\\
&amp;\eta^{2}\end{array}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>η</mi></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><msup><mi>η</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><msup><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>η</mi></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mo>]</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><mtext> or </mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd><mi>η</mi></mtd><mtd></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd></mtd><mtd><msup><mi>η</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mtd></mtr></mtable><mphantom></mphantom></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\eta&amp;\\
&amp;\eta^{-1}\end{array}\right],\left[\begin{array}[]{cc}\eta&amp;\\
