stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mn>32</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32\pi^{2}c_{1}^{2}(X)=\int_{X}s^{2}_{g_{\infty}}d\mu_{g_{\infty}}&lt;\int_{S^{4}/\Gamma_{k}}s^{2}_{g_{0}}d\mu_{g_{0}}=\frac{24\cdot 8\pi^{2}\chi(S^{4})}{|\Gamma_{k}|}=\frac{32\pi^{2}\cdot 12}{|\Gamma_{k}|},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.p8.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S4.p8.2.1" class="ltx_text">where
the inequality is necessarily strict because the <math id="S4.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Kähler-Einstein metric <math id="S4.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> cannot have constant sectional curvature.
The result thus follows, because <math id="S4.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(X)=(2\chi+3\tau)(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(X)=(2\chi+3\tau)(M)</annotation></semantics></math> by Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 4.2. ‣ 4 Constraints on Diffeotype ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.2</span></a>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S4.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Of course, Theorem <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> makes the stronger claim that this same conclusion actually holds if we merely assume that the limit
Einstein orbifold <math id="S4.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is <span id="S4.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Hermitian</span> — or equivalently, by Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Hermitian, Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>, that it is <span id="S4.p9.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">conformally Kähler</span>.
Moreover, once we have proved Theorem <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>, it will then follow that a Hermitian, Einstein orbifold limit of an admissible sequence <math id="S4.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})\to(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> can only
form singularities if <math id="S4.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(M)=c_{1}^{2}(X)\leq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(M)=c_{1}^{2}(X)\leq 4</annotation></semantics></math>; and, as we already know by Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Constraints on Diffeotype ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a>, the latter is equivalent to requiring that <math id="S4.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\approx{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#k\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\approx{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#k\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, where
<math id="S4.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5\leq k\leq 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5\leq k\leq 8</annotation></semantics></math>.
Indeed, the Odaka-Spotti-Sun classification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite> will then go on to predict that the limit of an admissible sequence can only
form singularities of the following types:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p10" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S4.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S4.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#5}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#5}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>: only <math id="S4.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math> singularities.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#6}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>6</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#6}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>: only <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> singularities.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#7}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>7</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#7}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>: only <math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, …, <math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{4}}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.I1.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\frac{1}{4}(1,1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\frac{1}{4}(1,1)}</annotation></semantics></math> singularities.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S4.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S4.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#8}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}}{\#8}{\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, …, <math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{A_{10}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{A_{10}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{D_{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{D_{4}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\frac{1}{4}(1,1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\frac{1}{4}(1,1)}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\frac{1}{8}(1,3)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\frac{1}{8}(1,3)}</annotation></semantics></math>, or
<math id="S4.I1.i4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\frac{1}{9}(1,2)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\frac{1}{9}(1,2)}</annotation></semantics></math> singularities.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S4.p10.1" class="ltx_p">This striking consequence helps illustrate the interest of Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Admissible Limits
and Desingularizations</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our key to understanding Gromov-Hausdorff convergence of admissible sequences of Einstein metrics is based on
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Corollary 4.16]</cite>, which we next present in a streamlined form that has been adapted to present purposes:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 5.1</span></span><span id="S5.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Ozuch)<span id="S5.Thmthm1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Given any positive real constant <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, there is a constant <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta=\delta(\nu)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta=\delta(\nu)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that,
whenever <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{\mathcal{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{\mathcal{E}})</annotation></semantics></math> is a smooth compact Einstein <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold with</span></p>
<ul id="S5.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">total volume </span><math id="S5.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq\nu</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ricci curvature </span><math id="S5.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">=3</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,</span></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and for which there is an Einstein <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-orbifold <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> with</span></p>
<table id="S5.Ex10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.Ex10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{GH}((M,g^{\mathcal{E}}),(X,g_{\infty}))&lt;\delta," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{GH}((M,g^{\mathcal{E}}),(X,g_{\infty}))&lt;\delta,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">then <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{\mathcal{E}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℰ</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{\mathcal{E}})</annotation></semantics></math> is obtained from <math id="S5.Thmthm1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> by the gluing-perturbation procedure detailed in §<a href="#S7" title="7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> below.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Here we have simplified the discussion by homothetically rescaling our <math id="S5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Einstein metrics in order to arrange for them
to have <math id="S5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=3</annotation></semantics></math>, which then guarantees, by Myers’ theorem, that they all have diameter <math id="S5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\leq\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≤</mo><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\leq\pi</annotation></semantics></math>. This simple observation
then guarantees that Theorem <a href="#S5.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 5.1 (Ozuch). ‣ 5 Admissible Limits and Desingularizations ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a> is a straightforward consequence of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Corollary 4.16]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The gluing-perturbation procedure cited in Theorem <a href="#S5.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 5.1 (Ozuch). ‣ 5 Admissible Limits and Desingularizations ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.1</span></a>
consists of first creating a smooth manifold by iteratively replacing each orbifold singularity with the corresponding the gravitational instanton that bubbles off,
and then equipping the resulting manifold with a family of so-called Einstein-modulo-obstruction metrics that satisfy a weakened form of the Einstein condition.
Following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, the manifolds that arise by this procedure will often be called <span id="S5.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">naïve desingularizations</span> of the original orbifold.
For a quantitative discussion of these technical points, see §<a href="#S7" title="7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> below.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In the absence of further information, however, the construction of naïve desingularizations depends on a detailed inventory
of the specific
trees of gravitational instantons that are to replace each orbifold singularity, along with scaling data that determines the relevant rates at which the
relevant gravitational instantons are to bubble off. However,
in the context of
admissible sequences, the allowed bubbling modes at each singularity actually form a single continuous family, and any
resulting desingularization therefore belongs to a single predetermined diffeotype, which the present paper’s second author has
elsewhere <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> called the
<span id="S5.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">expected topology</span>. Combining the framework of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, §5]</cite> with Theorem <a href="#S4.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 4.1. ‣ 4 Constraints on Diffeotype ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.1</span></a> therefore now provides us with the basic scaffolding
needed to support our proofs of Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S5.Thmthm2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 5.2</span></span><span id="S5.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S5.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be a compact Hermitian, Einstein orbifold with <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and only isolated singularities of
</span><span id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span><span id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">. Then there is a single family of naïve desingularizations of <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> by Einstein-modulo-obstruction manifolds diffeomorphic to a Del Pezzo surface such that any admissible sequence
<math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> of Einstein <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds that Gromov-Hausdorff converges to <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> consists, for sufficiently large <math id="S5.Thmthm2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,
of naïve desingularizations
that belong to this family.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>The Role of Wu’s Criterion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our proofs of Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> will also hinge on
showing that, for all <math id="S6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the Einstein manifolds <math id="S6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> must
everywhere satisfy
Wu’s criterion</p>
<table id="S6.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S6.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det(W^{+})&gt;0," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det(W^{+})&gt;0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S6.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the self-dual Weyl curvature <math id="S6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is considered as an endomorphism of the <math id="S6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>3</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional vector space <math id="S6.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda^{+}\subset\Lambda^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda^{+}\subset\Lambda^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> of self-dual
<math id="S6.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-forms at each point of <math id="S6.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>. As was first emphasized by Peng Wu <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>, this conformally-invariant condition is satisfied
by any conformally Kähler, Einstein metric on a Del Pezzo surface. Conversely, the first author <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> and Wu <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> proved,
by two entirely different methods,
that any Einstein metric on a compact simply-connected manifold that satisfies
(<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) everywhere must actually be conformally Kähler. Since (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) is an <span id="S6.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">open</span> condition, this in particular means that
smooth
Einstein perturbations of Hermitian, Einstein metrics always remain Hermitian. The gist of Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> is
essentially that the same also holds
for admissible sequences that merely tend, in the <span id="S6.p1.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Gromov-Hausdorff</span> sense, to an Einstein orbifold
that satisfies any of the equivalent conditions of Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Hermitian, Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a>.
To achieve this goal, we will use Proposition <a href="#S5.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 5.2. ‣ 5 Admissible Limits and Desingularizations ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5.2</span></a> to show that condition (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) continues to hold for such perturbations by carefully controlling the possible degenerations of Einstein
<math id="S6.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> in a manner that provides strong information regarding their curvature <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>.
Our proof will thus unfold in accordance with the following rough outline:</p>
<ol id="S6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(a)</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Construct suitable approximations <math id="S6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> of the Einstein metrics <math id="S6.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(b)</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Show that these approximations <math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy condition (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) for <math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(c)</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Show that condition (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) then also holds for the given <math id="S6.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="S6.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(d)</span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Invoke <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> to conclude that these <math id="S6.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> must therefore be Hermitian.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The rest of our article is therefore organized as follows. In Section <a href="#S7" title="7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>, we will review some key technical facts that underpin our
construction. In Section
<a href="#S8" title="8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a> we then
prove Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> in the prototypical case where there is only one singularity, and trees of singularities do not arise. In Section
<a href="#S9" title="9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>, we then generalize this to allow for multiple singularities, but still in the absence of
bubble-trees. Finally, in Section <a href="#S10" title="10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>, we prove our results in the most general but technically-challenging setting, where the formation of bubble-trees
is allowed.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall that the <span id="S7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein tensor</span> of a Riemannian <math id="S7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold <math id="S7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g)</annotation></semantics></math> is the symmetric tensor field defined by</p>
<table id="S7.Ex11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{E}=r-\frac{s}{2}g," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℰ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{E}=r-\frac{s}{2}g,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> are, respectively, the Ricci tensor and scalar curvature of <math id="S7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>; this definition is chosen so that the differential Bianchi identity
implies that <math id="S7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> is
automatically <span id="S7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">divergence-free</span> with respect to <math id="S7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>.
In the <math id="S7.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=4</annotation></semantics></math> case that is our sole concern here, the Einstein tensor takes the simple and attractive form</p>
<table id="S7.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{E}=\mathring{r}-\frac{s}{4}g" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℰ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{E}=\mathring{r}-\frac{s}{4}g</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.3" class="ltx_p">when expressed in terms of the trace-free part <math id="S7.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathring{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathring{r}</annotation></semantics></math> of the Ricci tensor <math id="S7.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>,
thereby allowing the Einstein equation</p>
<table id="S7.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\lambda g" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\lambda g</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.4" class="ltx_p">for a chosen Einstein constant <math id="S7.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math> to be rewritten as</p>
<table id="S7.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{E}+\lambda g=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℰ</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{E}+\lambda g=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.5" class="ltx_p">However, because of the diffeomorphism-invariance of the Einstein condition, this last equation fails to be elliptic. To remedy
this, we now choose some background metric <math id="S7.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, and then define a “gauged and normalized” version</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g_{0}}(g)=\mathscr{E}(g)+\lambda g+\delta_{g}^{*}\delta_{g_{0}}(g)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℰ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g_{0}}(g)=\mathscr{E}(g)+\lambda g+\delta_{g}^{*}\delta_{g_{0}}(g)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.6" class="ltx_p">of the Einstein tensor. On a compact manifold <math id="S7.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, the elliptic equation</p>
<table id="S7.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

</table>
<p id="S7.p1.7" class="ltx_p">is then equivalent to the pair of conditions</p>

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S7.E4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=0," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=0,</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S7.p1.8" class="ltx_p">Indeed, since <math id="S7.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{g}\mathscr{E}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℰ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{g}\mathscr{E}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, applying <math id="S7.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> to (<a href="#S7.E3" title="In 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>) yields <math id="S7.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{g}\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{g}\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and this then implies that</p>
<table id="S7.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\|\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g\|^{2}\,d\mu_{g}=\int_{M}\langle\delta_{g_{0}}g,\,\delta_{g}\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g\rangle\,d\mu_{g}=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><msup><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.337em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\|\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g\|^{2}\,d\mu_{g}=\int_{M}\langle\delta_{g_{0}}g,\,\delta_{g}\delta^{*}_{g}\delta_{g_{0}}g\rangle\,d\mu_{g}=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.p1.9" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="S7.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ker\delta_{g}^{*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ker</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msubsup><mi>δ</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ker\delta_{g}^{*}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly consists of the Killing fields on <math id="S7.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g)</annotation></semantics></math>, equation
(<a href="#S7.E5" title="In 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>) is equivalent to saying that <math id="S7.p1.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{g_{0}}g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{g_{0}}g</annotation></semantics></math> is a Killing field of <math id="S7.p1.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>.
This formalism becomes particularly elegant and natural if <math id="S7.p1.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is known, for some <span id="S7.p1.9.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">a priori</span> reason, to have discrete isometry group,
and the reader is therefore invited to provisionally focus on the case in which neither the limit orbifold nor the smooth metrics in the given sequence admit any Killing vector fields. However, the presence of Killing fields merely leads to a mild failure in uniqueness when representing
a given Einstein geometry by a solution of (<a href="#S7.E3" title="In 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>). While this will have no impact on the regularity-type results that are our goal here,
the interested reader may wish to consult <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> for further discussion of this issue.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In dimension four,
a straightforward (albeit tedious) calculation shows that
the linearization

of (<a href="#S7.E2" title="In 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>) at <math id="S7.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is the elliptic operator</p>

are all defined with respect to <math id="S7.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>; here <math id="S7.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Hess" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Hess</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Hess</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=d^{*}d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=d^{*}d</annotation></semantics></math> respectively denote the Hessian and positive-spectrum Laplacian on scalar-valued functions,
while the Riemann curvature tensor acts on symmetric <math id="S7.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors by</p>

<p id="S7.p2.3" class="ltx_p">In particular, when <math id="S7.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is Einstein, with Einstein constant <math id="S7.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>,
and when the symmetric <math id="S7.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor is <math id="S7.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is traceless and divergence-free, the
linearization <math id="S7.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{P}_{g_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>P</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{P}_{g_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> then reduces to</p>

<p id="S7.p2.4" class="ltx_p">or, in other words, half the Lichnerowicz Laplacian <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, p. 54]</cite> of <math id="S7.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
