<div id="S7.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text"></span>
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="S7.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark<span id="S7.p3.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_medium"> </span></span> Of course, these operators can naturally be defined on symmetric <math id="S7.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors belonging to various function spaces.
On orbifolds, ALE spaces and their gluings, the theory developed in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> actually considers them in the function spaces <math id="S7.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.p3.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,**}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,**}</annotation></semantics></math> described in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Function Spaces ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In order to begin implementing this last remark, we now focus on the case of an oriented <math id="S7.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional
orbifold <math id="S7.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> with only finitely many singularities, all of <span id="S7.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span>. Recall that, according to Definition <a href="#Thmdefn2" title="Definition 2. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>,
this means that each singular point <math id="S7.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}\in X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}\in X</annotation></semantics></math> has a neighborhood modeled on a neighborhood of the origin in a
quotient <math id="S7.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{R}}^{4}/\Gamma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{k}&lt;SO(4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{k}&lt;SO(4)</annotation></semantics></math>,
that also occurs as the tangent-cone-at-infinity of some Ricci-flat ALE manifold with <math id="S7.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\equiv 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>≡</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\equiv 0</annotation></semantics></math>. We also remind the reader that a
complete list of the <math id="S7.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> allowed by this definition is provided by Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 2.1. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>. Now notice that Definition <a href="#Thmdefn2" title="Definition 2. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>
tells us that it
makes sense to modify <math id="S7.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> by cutting out a neighborhood of <math id="S7.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}\in X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}\in X</annotation></semantics></math> and replacing it with an anti-self-dual Ricci-flat ALE manifold.
In order to carry out this procedure in a systematic way, we will next establish some conventions for doing so.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 3</span></span><span id="Thmdefn3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(The function <math id="Thmdefn3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{o}</annotation></semantics></math> on an orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be a complete oriented <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional orbifold with only finitely many isolated singularities.
Choose an <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{0}\in(0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{0}\in(0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> such that the Riemannian <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>-distance ball <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}=B_{\epsilon_{0}}(p_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}=B_{\epsilon_{0}}(p_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> around each singular point <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is orientedly diffeomorphic, via the exponential map, to <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B^{4}/\Gamma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>B</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B^{4}/\Gamma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for
some finite group <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma_{k}&lt;{SO}(4)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>O</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma_{k}&lt;{SO}(4)</annotation></semantics></math> that acts freely on <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S^{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>S</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S^{3}</annotation></semantics></math>.
We then choose a smooth function <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{o}:X\to[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{o}:X\to[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> which, on each <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, coincides with the Riemannian distance
from the singular point <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, and which satisfies <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{o}\geq\epsilon_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{o}\geq\epsilon_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> on the complement of the union of the <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. For every
<math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\in(0,\epsilon_{0})</annotation></semantics></math>, we then also set</span></p>
<table id="S7.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X(\epsilon):=\varrho_{o}^{-1}[\epsilon,1]=X-\Big(\bigcup_{k}B_{\epsilon}(p_{k})\Big)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0em" movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mi>k</mi></munder><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X(\epsilon):=\varrho_{o}^{-1}[\epsilon,1]=X-\Big(\bigcup_{k}B_{\epsilon}(p_{k})\Big)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmdefn3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{\epsilon}(p_{k})\subset U_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>ϵ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{\epsilon}(p_{k})\subset U_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the radius-<math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϵ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math> Riemannian distance ball about <math id="Thmdefn3.p1.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Next, we define <math id="S7.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> to be the space of traceless, divergence-free symmetric <math id="S7.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors on a <math id="S7.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional manifold or orbifold with metric <math id="S7.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>
that belong to the kernel of <math id="S7.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{g_{\infty}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{g_{\infty}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Then, as explained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 5]</cite>, there is a one-to-one map from a neighborhood of <math id="S7.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> to the moduli space of <span id="S7.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein-modulo-obstructions</span> perturbations of <math id="S7.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> defined by (<a href="#S7.E3" title="In 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>):</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S7.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 7.1</span></span><span id="S7.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S7.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{o}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{o}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>, there is a unique metric <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying:</span></p>
<ol id="S7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty}),</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-g_{\infty}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}\leqslant C\|v_{o}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup></msub><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-g_{\infty}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}\leqslant C\|v_{o}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-(g_{\infty}+v_{o})\perp_{L^{2}(g_{\infty})}\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo>⟂</mo><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>𝔒</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-(g_{\infty}+v_{o})\perp_{L^{2}(g_{\infty})}\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for some <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.
In what follows, this metric <math id="S7.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> will be called an Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p6.1" class="ltx_p">We next recall some important key facts regarding ALE Ricci-flat metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 4</span></span><span id="Thmdefn4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(The function <math id="Thmdefn4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> on an ALE orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">We define <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> a smooth function on <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}:=(\Psi_{k})_{*}\rho_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>𝛅</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}:=(\Psi_{k})_{*}\rho_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}</annotation></semantics></math> on each <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}:=(\Psi_{\infty})_{*}\rho_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mi>𝛅</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}:=(\Psi_{\infty})_{*}\rho_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\infty}=N-K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\infty}=N-K</annotation></semantics></math>, and such that <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon_{0}\leqslant\varrho_{b}\leqslant\epsilon_{0}^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>⩽</mo><msubsup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon_{0}\leqslant\varrho_{b}\leqslant\epsilon_{0}^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> on the rest of <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>.
For <math id="Thmdefn4.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\epsilon\leqslant\epsilon_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\epsilon\leqslant\epsilon_{0}</annotation></semantics></math>, we then set</span></p>
<table id="S7.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" </div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we define <math id="S7.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> to be the space of infinitesimal Einstein deformations of <math id="S7.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> which are traceless and divergence-free.
As is explained in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 5]</cite>, there is a one-to-one map from a neighborhood of <math id="S7.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> to the moduli space of K”ahler <span id="S7.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Ricci-flat ALE metrics</span> perturbations of <math id="S7.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 5</span></span><span id="Thmdefn5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each <math id="Thmdefn5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{b}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{b}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math>, and for a suitable <math id="Thmdefn5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, we let <math id="Thmdefn5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote
the unique Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric satisfying:</span></p>
<ol id="S7.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S7.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g_{b}}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g_{b}}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})=0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g_{b}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}}\leqslant C\|v_{b}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}}^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup></msub><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g_{b}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}}\leqslant C\|v_{b}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}}^{2}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S7.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="[\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-(g_{b}+v_{b})]\perp_{L^{2}(g_{b})}\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><msub><mo>⟂</mo><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mi>𝔒</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-(g_{b}+v_{b})]\perp_{L^{2}(g_{b})}\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p8.1" class="ltx_p">We next review the notion of a naïve desingularization of an orbifold, which played a crucial role in the results of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Gluing of ALE spaces to orbifold singularities.</h5>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;2\epsilon&lt;\epsilon_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;2\epsilon&lt;\epsilon_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> be a fixed constant, <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> an orbifold and <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Phi:B_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(0,\epsilon_{0})\subset\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma\to U" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>U</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Phi:B_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(0,\epsilon_{0})\subset\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma\to U</annotation></semantics></math> the inverse of a local chart around a singular point <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in Y</annotation></semantics></math>. Let also <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> be an ALE orbifold asymptotic to <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Psi:(\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma)-B_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(0,\epsilon_{0}^{-1})\to N-K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Psi:(\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma)-B_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(0,\epsilon_{0}^{-1})\to N-K</annotation></semantics></math> the inverse of an orbifold chart at infinity.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">

rescaling map <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\to\mathsf{s}x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mi>𝗌</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\to\mathsf{s}x</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t&lt;\epsilon_{0}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msubsup><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t&lt;\epsilon_{0}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, we then define <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\#N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\#N</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> glued to <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math> via the diffeomorphism</p>

supported in <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,2]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,2]</annotation></semantics></math> and equal to <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>

<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 6</span></span><span id="Thmdefn6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Naïve gluing of an ALE space to an orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn6.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be an Einstein orbifold, and <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{D})</annotation></semantics></math> a naïve desingularization of <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> by a tree of ALE Ricci-flat orbifolds <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N_{j},g_{b_{j}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N_{j},g_{b_{j}})</annotation></semantics></math> glued at scales <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{j}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{j}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Here, the manifold <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is also covered as <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=Y^{t}\cup\bigcup_{j}N_{j}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><mo rspace="0.055em">∪</mo><mrow><msub><mo>⋃</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=Y^{t}\cup\bigcup_{j}N_{j}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, where</p>

</table>
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is the relative gluing scale of <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> at the singular point <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}\in Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}\in Y</annotation></semantics></math>, and where</p>

<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.3" class="ltx_p">On <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{16t}\subset Y^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{16t}\subset Y^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}=g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}=g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> and on each <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{j}^{16t}\subset N_{j}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mrow><mn>16</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>⊂</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{j}^{16t}\subset N_{j}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}=T_{j}g_{b_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}=T_{j}g_{b_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math>. We also define <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{\max}:=\max_{j}t_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>max</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>max</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{\max}:=\max_{j}t_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>. By Definition <a href="#Thmdefn6" title="Definition 6 (Naïve gluing of an ALE space to an orbifold). ‣ Gluing of ALE spaces to orbifold singularities. ‣ 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>, on the intersection <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{j}^{t}\cap Y^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo>∩</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{j}^{t}\cap Y^{t}</annotation></semantics></math> we then have <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}=\varrho_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}=\varrho_{o}</annotation></semantics></math>, and on the intersection <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{j}^{t}\cap N_{k}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><mo>∩</mo><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{j}^{t}\cap N_{k}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}=\sqrt{T_{k}}r_{b_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}=\sqrt{T_{k}}r_{b_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 7</span></span><span id="Thmdefn7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Function <math id="Thmdefn7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> on a naïve desingularization)<span id="Thmdefn7.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">On a naïve desingularization <math id="Thmdefn7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{D})</annotation></semantics></math>, we define a function <math id="Thmdefn7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> in the following way:</span></p>
<ol id="S7.I3" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S7.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S7.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}=\varrho_{o}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}=\varrho_{o}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> on </span><math id="S7.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>Y</mi><mi>t</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{t}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I3.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S7.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S7.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}=\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msqrt><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msqrt><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}=\sqrt{T_{j}}r_{b_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> on each </span><math id="S7.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{j}^{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{j}^{t}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S7.I3.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="Thmdefn7.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn7.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The function <math id="Thmdefn7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> is then smooth on <math id="Thmdefn7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn8" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn8.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 8</span></span><span id="Thmdefn8.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Expected topology)<span id="Thmdefn8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn8.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn8.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A desingularization <math id="Thmdefn8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{D}_{t,v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{D}_{t,v})</annotation></semantics></math> of a conformally Kähler, Einstein orbifold <math id="Thmdefn8.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is said to have the expected topology if the Ricci-flat ALE spaces
used to construct the
desingularization are all Kähler, in an orientation-compatible manner.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Notice that the notion of expected topology therefore exactly models the sort of singularity formation that can arise from an admissible sequence in the sense of Definition <a href="#Thmdefn1" title="Definition 1. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>, and so
in particular only applies
to singularities of <span id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">type T</span> in the sense of Definition <a href="#Thmdefn2" title="Definition 2. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Simplest Case of the Proof</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will now illustrate our strategy by proving Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> in the simple case where <math id="S8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> only has one singularity, and no bubble-trees arise.</p>
</div>
<section id="S8.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics</h3>

<div id="S8.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As was shown in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>, around a singular point <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, we can find a coordinate system on <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> in which we have an expansion of a solution of <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}(\bar{g}_{v_{\infty}})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>δ</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}(\bar{g}_{v_{\infty}})=0</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\boldsymbol{\delta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>𝜹</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\boldsymbol{\delta}}</annotation></semantics></math> the Euclidean metric, and</p>

<p id="S8.SSx1.p1.4" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma:=p^{-1}(\{0\})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>p</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma:=p^{-1}(\{0\})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p:N\mapsto\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo stretchy="false">↦</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p:N\mapsto\mathbb{C}^{2}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> the minimal resolution if <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma&lt;SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma&lt;SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math>, or its image in the appropriate quotient if <math id="S8.SSx1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\not&lt;SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>≮</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\not&lt;SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In the rest of the section, we will construct what we call an <span id="S8.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">approximate obstruction space</span> (an approximate co-kernel of the linearization of the Einstein equation) and an approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions desingularization.</p>
</div>
<section id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Extension of obstructions</h4>

<div id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}=\mathfrak{w}_{0}+\mathfrak{w}_{2}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{o}^{3})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐰</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi><mn>3</mn></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{w}=\mathfrak{w}_{0}+\mathfrak{w}_{2}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{o}^{3})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathfrak{w}_{i}|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}\leqslant\varrho_{o}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo>⩽</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathfrak{w}_{i}|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}\leqslant\varrho_{o}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{o}=O^{4}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{o}^{-5})\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔬</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>O</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{o}=O^{4}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{o}^{-5})\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})</annotation></semantics></math>.
As proven in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, Lemma 2.7]</cite>, there is a unique tensor <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying: for <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> of (<a href="#S8.E13" title="In Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>),</p>

<p id="S8.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">and a symmetric <math id="S8.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor <math id="S8.I1.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{4}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.I1.i5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.I1.i5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mho_{4}\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mho_{4}\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying the following equations</p>
</div>

<div id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof of the existence of the above tensors.</h6>
<div id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof of the existence and uniqueness of solutions of (<a href="#S8.E18" title="In item 1 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>), (<a href="#S8.E21" title="In item 4 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>) and (<a href="#S8.E22" title="In item 5 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>) are exactly as in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>, which did not depend on any peculiar features of the Eguchi-Hanson metric.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let us first give a proof for the existence of <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying (<a href="#S8.E19" title="In item 2 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>). Here
the <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{H}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{H}_{3}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}\mathfrak{H}_{3}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}\mathfrak{H}_{3}=0</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> so <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}_{3})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}_{3})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-3})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> since <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-{\boldsymbol{\delta}}=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>𝜹</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-{\boldsymbol{\delta}}=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-4})</annotation></semantics></math>. From <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Lemma 4.3]</cite>, it is possible to find <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}h^{\prime}=-P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}_{3})" display="inline" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}_{3})\perp_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" Now, by integration by parts: for <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mho}_{v_{b}}\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mho}_{v_{b}}\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>

<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Indeed, the boundary term is proportional to <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" but the coefficients of <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{H}_{3}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><annotation intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ϱ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>, hence their restrictions on <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> belong to different eigenspaces of the spherical Laplacian and therefore are orthogonal:</span></p>
<table id="S8.Ex40" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex40.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}\langle\mathfrak{H}_{3},\mathfrak{H}^{4}\rangle_{g_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}}d\mu_{g_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}}=0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><msup><mi>𝕊</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}\langle\mathfrak{H}_{3},\mathfrak{H}^{4}\rangle_{g_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}}d\mu_{g_{\mathbb{S}^{3}/\Gamma}}=0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.3.1" class="ltx_text">Here, the existence of <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{H}_{3}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{H}_{3}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is proved exactly as in the proof of the existence of <math id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{H}_{2}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{H}_{2}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, Lemma 2.3]</cite>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx1.SSSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">We now define the approximate-solution metrics we will need.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn10" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn10.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 10</span></span><span id="Thmdefn10.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn10.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">When <math id="Thmdefn10.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v=(v_{o},v_{b})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>v</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v=(v_{o},v_{b})\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmdefn10.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> are both sufficiently small, we use the conventions of Definition <a href="#Thmdefn6" title="Definition 6 (Naïve gluing of an ALE space to an orbifold). ‣ Gluing of ALE spaces to orbifold singularities. ‣ 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>
to define the approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric as the naïve desingularization</span></p>
</div>
