<section id="S8.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Control of the approximate solutions</h3>

<div id="S8.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The metrics <math id="S8.SSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> solve the <span id="S8.SSx2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein-modulo-obstructions</span> equation in a manner that allows us to
naturally extend the estimate <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, equation (50)]</cite> as follows:</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 8.1</span></span><span id="S8.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\beta&lt;\frac{1}{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\beta&lt;\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S8.E23" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.E23.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D}_{t,v}}(g^{A}_{t,v})+\mho^{A}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D}_{t})}=o(t)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mi>α</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D}_{t,v}}(g^{A}_{t,v})+\mho^{A}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D}_{t})}=o(t)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(23)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">as <math id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g^{A}_{t,v}-g^{D}_{t}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t})}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g^{A}_{t,v}-g^{D}_{t}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t})}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S8.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to(0,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to(0,0)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S8.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof of this estimate is very similar to those in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>. We will focus here on
the most challenging aspect of the proof, which pertains to the region <math id="S8.SSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{o}&lt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{o}&lt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S8.SSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{-\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;2t^{-\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{-\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;2t^{-\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math>
where the cut-off is used. Here one has</span></p>
<table id="S8.Ex43" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex43.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}={\boldsymbol{\delta}}+\mathfrak{H}_{2}+\mathfrak{H}_{3}+\mathfrak{H}_{4}+t^{2}\mathfrak{H}^{4}+t^{2}\mathfrak{H}^{4}_{2}+t^{2}\mathfrak{H}^{4}_{3}+t^{2}\mathfrak{H}^{4}_{4}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{5})+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{o}^{5-\epsilon}\varrho_{b}^{-4})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" <p id="S8.SSx2.p2.4" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx2.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">Together with the controls on the cut-off function, this shows that (<a href="#S8.E23" title="In Proposition 8.1. ‣ Control of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>) is satisfied in the annulus <math id="S8.SSx2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{o}&lt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{o}&lt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S8.SSx2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{-\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;2t^{-\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{-\frac{1}{4}}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;2t^{-\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The proof for the other regions is easier, and can be found in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>.
∎</span></p>

<section id="S8.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Curvature of the approximate solutions</h3>

<div id="S8.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>i</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> be canonical coordinate functions on <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{1}^{0}=dx^{1}\wedge dx^{2}+dx^{3}\wedge dx^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{1}^{0}=dx^{1}\wedge dx^{2}+dx^{3}\wedge dx^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{1}^{0}=dx^{1}\wedge dx^{2}-dx^{3}\wedge dx^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo dx^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, and similarly <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math>. On <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, we denote <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> the hyper-Kähler forms asymptotic to <math id="S8.SSx3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The following proofs rely on the isomorphism between <math id="S8.SSx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda^{-}_{g_{b}}\otimes\Lambda^{+}_{g_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>−</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>+</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda^{-}_{g_{b}}\otimes\Lambda^{+}_{g_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> and traceless <math id="S8.SSx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors obtained as follows: identifying <math id="S8.SSx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors and endomorphisms of <math id="S8.SSx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="TM" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">TM</annotation></semantics></math>, the composition of endomorphisms <math id="S8.SSx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega^{-}\circ\omega^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ω</mi><mo>−</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msup><mi>ω</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega^{-}\circ\omega^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> is symmetric traceless.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 8.2</span></span><span id="S8.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> be a constant <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor on <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> projected on <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\subset SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\subset SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math>.
Then, for <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math> there exists <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{i}\in\Lambda^{-}_{g_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>−</mo></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{i}\in\Lambda^{-}_{g_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\Theta_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\Theta_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> of (<a href="#S8.E15" title="In Extension of obstructions ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">15</span></a>) is equal to <math id="S8.Thmthm2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{i}\Theta_{i}\circ\omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{i}\Theta_{i}\circ\omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">Let <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> be a <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor on <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> obtained from <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, Lemma 2.7]</cite> asymptotic to a constant traceless <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}=\sum_{i,j}\mathfrak{w}_{0,ij}\theta_{j}^{0}\otimes\omega_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>j</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}=\sum_{i,j}\mathfrak{w}_{0,ij}\theta_{j}^{0}\otimes\omega_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0,ij}\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0,ij}\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the above <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{j}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>j</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{j}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}^{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}^{0}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\theta_{i}^{0}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\theta_{i}^{0}=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\omega_{i}^{0}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\omega_{i}^{0}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is traceless, there are anti-self-dual <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-forms <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}=\sum_{i}\Theta_{i}\circ\omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}=\sum_{i}\Theta_{i}\circ\omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="dd^{*}\Theta_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">dd^{*}\Theta_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{i}=\sum_{j}W_{0,ij}\theta_{j}^{0}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{-4})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>θ</mi><mi>j</mi><mn>0</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϱ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{i}=\sum_{j}W_{0,ij}\theta_{j}^{0}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{-4})</annotation></semantics></math>. By integration by parts, this yields:</span></p>

<p id="S8.SSx3.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">Now, <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{*}\Theta_{i}\wedge\Theta_{i}=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-5})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{*}\Theta_{i}\wedge\Theta_{i}=\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-5})</annotation></semantics></math> so the boundary term vanishes, and <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d^{*}\Theta_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>d</mi><mo>∗</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d^{*}\Theta_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Theta_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Theta_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is anti-self-dual , this implies <math id="S8.SSx3.p3.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\Theta_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Θ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\Theta_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Let us now extend <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, Lemma 8]</cite> to the general setting in which the obstructions do not all happen to vanish.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 8.3</span></span><span id="S8.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> be an ALE Ricci-flat Kähler metric, and <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> as in (<a href="#S8.E18" title="In item 1 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>).
Then, the first order variation</span></p>
<table id="S8.Ex53" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex53.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{+,(1)}_{g_{b}}(h_{2})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mrow><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{+,(1)}_{g_{b}}(h_{2})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">in the direction of <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> of the self-dual curvature <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> has constant eigenvalues equal to those of <math id="S8.Thmthm3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}_{\bar{g}_{v_{o}}}^{+}(p)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>p</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}_{\bar{g}_{v_{o}}}^{+}(p)</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.2" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Since the assertion is essentially local in nature, we may pass, if necessary, to a finite cover of the relevant ALE space, and thereby arrange for it to be
hyper-Kähler, as in the proof of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Corollary 6.4]</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">The proof of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, Lemma 8]</cite> using <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>, Lemma 3]</cite> now immediately extends to show that <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathring{r}^{(1)}_{g_{b}}(h_{2})=\sum_{i}\Omega_{i}\circ\omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>i</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathring{r}^{(1)}_{g_{b}}(h_{2})=\sum_{i}\Omega_{i}\circ\omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> anti-self-dual <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-forms satisfying <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\Omega_{i}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\Omega_{i}=0</annotation></semantics></math> and asymptotically constant (or decaying at infinity), and <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> the three Kähler forms on <math id="S8.SSx3.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>. This is exactly our situation by Lemma <a href="#S8.Thmthm2" title="Lemma 8.2. ‣ Curvature of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.2</span></a>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We can therefore precise our estimate of the curvature of these metrics:</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S8.Thmthm4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 8.4</span></span><span id="S8.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S8.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">The self-dual Weyl curvature <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> at any point has eigenvalues arbitrarily close to those of <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> at some corresponding point of <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, up to an error that tends to zero uniformly as <math id="S8.Thmthm4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.3" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text">On the region <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{o}&gt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{o}&gt;2t^{\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-g_{\infty})|\leqslant C\|v_{o}\|_{C^{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}}-g_{\infty})|\leqslant C\|v_{o}\|_{C^{2}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{2}|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}h^{4}|\leqslant t^{1-\frac{l}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>l</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{2}|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}h^{4}|\leqslant t^{1-\frac{l}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Consequently, when <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v_{o})\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v_{o})\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}-g_{\infty})|\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\nabla^{l}_{g_{\infty}}(\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}-g_{\infty})|\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l&lt;4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l&lt;4</annotation></semantics></math>, and in particular, the self-dual Weyl curvature of <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}+t^{2}h^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> uniformly tends to that of <math id="S8.SSx3.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> in this region.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx3.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p9.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p9.1.1" class="ltx_text">For <math id="S8.SSx3.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> small enough independent of <math id="S8.SSx3.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)</annotation></semantics></math>, on the region <math id="S8.SSx3.p9.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\delta^{-1}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;t^{-1/4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>ϱ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta^{-1}&lt;\varrho_{b}&lt;t^{-1/4}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S8.SSx3.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{t}g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{b}}+th_{2}+t^{\frac{3}{2}}h_{3}+t^{2}h_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{b}}+th_{2}+t^{\frac{3}{2}}h_{3}+t^{2}h_{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</span></p>
<table id="S8.Ex54" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S8.SSx3.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p10.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p10.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, on the region <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}&lt;\delta^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}&lt;\delta^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{1}{t}g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{b}}+th_{2}+t^{\frac{3}{2}}h_{3}+t^{2}h_{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>t</mi></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>4</mn></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{t}g^{A}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{b}}+th_{2}+t^{\frac{3}{2}}h_{3}+t^{2}h_{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\leqslant 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\leqslant 3</annotation></semantics></math>, we have
<math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\frac{i}{2}}|\nabla^{l}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}h_{i}|\leqslant Ct^{\frac{i}{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>t</mi><mfrac><mi>i</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\frac{i}{2}}|\nabla^{l}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}h_{i}|\leqslant Ct^{\frac{i}{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> independent of <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S8.SSx3.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>v</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v</annotation></semantics></math> small enough. We therefore have</span></p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex57.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}(g^{A}_{t,v})=W^{+,(1)}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(h_{2})+\mathsf{O}(t)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}(g^{A}_{t,v})=W^{+,(1)}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(h_{2})+\mathsf{O}(t).</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<div id="S8.SSx3.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx3.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.SSx3.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text">However, because the Einstein orbifold <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is assumed to be limit of an admissible sequence of <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Einstein metrics, <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{+}(g_{\infty})=\frac{s}{12}g_{\infty}+W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{+}(g_{\infty})=\frac{s}{12}g_{\infty}+W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> must
have zero as an eigenvalue at the singular point <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math> by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, which refined an earlier result of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>. However, since Theorem <a href="#S3.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 3.1. ‣ 3 Hermitian, Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.1</span></a> tells us <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> is conformal
to a Kähler metric of positive scalar curvature, the two smallest eigenvalues of the trace-free tensor <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> are everywhere equal, it therefore follows that
<math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{+}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{+}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> has eigenvalues <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,0,\frac{s}{4})=(0,0,\lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mi>s</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,0,\frac{s}{4})=(0,0,\lambda)</annotation></semantics></math> at the singular point <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>p</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p</annotation></semantics></math>. By Lemma <a href="#S8.Thmthm3" title="Lemma 8.3. ‣ Curvature of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.3</span></a>, it therefore follows that
<math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}^{+,(1)}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(h_{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mo rspace="0em">+</mo><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}^{+,(1)}_{\bar{g}_{v_{b}}}(h_{2})</annotation></semantics></math> has eigenvalues arbitrarily close to <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(0,0,\lambda)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>λ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(0,0,\lambda)</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>. The eigenvalues of <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> therefore tend to <math id="S8.SSx3.p11.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(-\frac{\lambda}{3},-\frac{\lambda}{3},\frac{2\lambda}{3})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mi>λ</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>,</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>λ</mi></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(-\frac{\lambda}{3},-\frac{\lambda}{3},\frac{2\lambda}{3})</annotation></semantics></math>
in this region, and the claim therefore holds everywhere. ∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S8.SSx4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a></h3>

<div id="S8.SSx4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Now suppose that <math id="S8.SSx4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is a conformally Kähler, Einstein orbifold with <math id="S8.SSx4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda=3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda=3</annotation></semantics></math>, with <span id="S8.SSx4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">exactly one</span> singularity, for which there is an admissible sequence <math id="S8.SSx4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math>
with</p>
<table id="S8.Ex58" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S8.Ex58.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{GH}\Big((M,g_{i}),(X,g_{\infty})\Big)\to 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{GH}\Big((M,g_{i}),(X,g_{\infty})\Big)\to 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S8.SSx4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Furthermore, assume that any Ricci-flat ALE rescaled pointed limit that bubbles off from the sequence has no orbifold singularities.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.SSx4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.SSx4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, then, after possibly passing to a subsequence, there then exist scales <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, naïve desingularizations <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and parameters <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> such that</p>
<ul id="S8.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S8.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S8.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S8.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g_{i}-g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g_{i}-g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S8.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S8.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g_{i}-g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\perp_{g^{D}_{tj}}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><msub><mo>⟂</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}-g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\perp_{g^{D}_{tj}}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>

<p id="S8.SSx4.p2.3" class="ltx_p">as <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>, by virtue of (<a href="#S8.E23" title="In Proposition 8.1. ‣ Control of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>). This then allows us to obtain the following curvature-control: for some <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, independent of <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
