<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(24)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S8.SSx4.p2.4" class="ltx_p">as <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\to\infty" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\to\infty</annotation></semantics></math>,
since, by definition of the norms: <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\cdot\|_{C^{0}(g_{i})}\;\leqslant\;Ct_{i}^{-1}\|\cdot\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mn>0</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.558em">⩽</mo><mi>C</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>i</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∥</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mi>α</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\cdot\|_{C^{0}(g_{i})}\;\leqslant\;Ct_{i}^{-1}\|\cdot\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}</annotation></semantics></math> because <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}^{2}&gt;t_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}^{2}&gt;t_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
However, because <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det(W^{+})(g_{\infty})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det(W^{+})(g_{\infty})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> everywhere,Corollary <a href="#S8.Thmthm4" title="Corollary 8.4. ‣ Curvature of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> implies
that <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det\operatorname{W}^{+}(g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">det</mo><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det\operatorname{W}^{+}(g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>. By (<a href="#S8.E24" title="In Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems and ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>), the open property
<math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det\operatorname{W}^{+}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">det</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det\operatorname{W}^{+}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is therefore inherited by the genuine Einstein metrics <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for sufficiently large <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. We have thus shown that
the Einstein metrics <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy Wu’s criterion (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), so it follows <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> that the <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> must be <span id="S8.SSx4.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">conformally Kähler</span>
when <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>. However, such Einstein metrics on smooth <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds are actually all
Kähler-Einstein, aside <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, Theorem A]</cite> from two strongly-rigid exceptions for which, up to isometries and rescalings, there is only one conformally-Kähler Einstein manifold on the given <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold; but this rigid scenario
is then precluded by our assumption that the limit has an orbifold singularity.
We have thus shown that Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> do in fact hold in the test-case where <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> has exactly one singularity, and no trees of singularities occur.
 <math id="S8.SSx4.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9 </span>Without Trees of Singularities</h2>

<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now allow multiple singularities, but exclude the formation of
trees of singularities. For example, as explained in Corollary <a href="#S9.Thmthm2" title="Corollary 9.2. ‣ Conclusion of the proof ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9.2</span></a> below,
this applies to desingularizations of a Kähler-Einstein orbifolds with <math id="S9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}=4</annotation></semantics></math>.
In general terms, this case is very similar to the situation discussed in §<a href="#S8" title="8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, and can best be understood using the framework of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 5.2]</cite> through the use
of <span id="S9.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">partial</span> Einstein-modulo-obstructions desingularizations.
Roughly speaking, the idea is to desingularize the singularities one-by-one, from the smallest scale to the largest one. <span id="S9.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">A priori</span>, one can only partially desingularize by Einstein-modulo-obstruction metrics. Starting by the smallest scale is crucial as it ensures negligible perturbations of the orbifold at its remaining singular points.

<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let us once again take <math id="S9.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> to be an admissible sequence of Einstein metrics that converges to a conformally Kähler, Einstein orbifold <math id="S9.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> in the Gromov-Hausdorff sense.
We now allow <math id="S9.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> to possibly have <span id="S9.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">multiple</span> singularities, but we still suppose trees of singularities do not occur. As in the previous Section <a href="#S8.SSx4" title="Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems and ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, then, up to taking a subsequence, for <math id="S9.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> large enough, there exists a naïve desingularization <math id="S9.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> and parameters <math id="S9.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})</annotation></semantics></math> such that:
<math id="S9.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g_{i}-g^{D}_{t_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g_{i}-g^{D}_{t_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
As in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 5.2]</cite>, we will produce a better approximate metrics <math id="S9.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t_{i},v_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> by using <span id="S9.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">partial</span> Einstein-modulo-obstructions desingularizations as stepping stones.</p>
</div>
<section id="S9.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Iterative partial naïve desingularizations</h3>

<div id="S9.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">After passing to a subsequence, we may assume that we can order the <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> singular points of <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},...,p_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},...,p_{n}</annotation></semantics></math> so that</p>
<table id="S9.Ex60" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S9.Ex60.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;t_{1,i}\leqslant t_{2,i}\leqslant...\leqslant t_{n,i}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⩽</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;t_{1,i}\leqslant t_{2,i}\leqslant...\leqslant t_{n,i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S9.SSx1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k,i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the scale of the gluing at <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> in the construction of <math id="S9.SSx1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A}_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>A</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A}_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> in Definition <a href="#Thmdefn10" title="Definition 10. ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn11" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 11</span></span><span id="Thmdefn11.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Partial naïve desingularizations)<span id="Thmdefn11.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn11.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn11.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{1,...,n\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{1,...,n\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k^{\rm th}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>k</mi><mi>th</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k^{\rm th}</annotation></semantics></math> <em id="Thmdefn11.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_upright">partial</em> desingularization of <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>, which we will denote by <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(Y_{k},g^{D_{k}}_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(Y_{k},g^{D_{k}}_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, is obtained by the naïve gluing of <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, …, <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> at the corresponding points <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>,…, <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> at the scales <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>,…, <math id="Thmdefn11.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S9.SSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By iteration on <math id="S9.SSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, we can then define approximate-Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics <math id="S9.SSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and <span id="S9.SSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_sansserif">actual</span> Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics <math id="S9.SSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S9.SSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> as follows:</p>
</div>
<section id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">For <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0</annotation></semantics></math>,</h5>

<div id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">we define <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}):=\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}):=\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Now let <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>⩽</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</h5>

<div id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The idea is to replace <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})</annotation></semantics></math> and to perform the constructions as in Section <a href="#S8" title="8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">

<p id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Now, by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Theorem 4.10]</cite>, there exists a unique Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying: for <math id="S9.SSx1.SSS0.Px2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)</annotation></semantics></math> small enough,</p>

</div></li>
<li id="S9.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S9.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}_{t}}(\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v})\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}_{t}}(\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v})\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S9.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Controlling the approximate desingularizations</h3>

<div id="S9.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As in the proof of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, (96), Proposition 5.13]</cite>, the proof of Proposition <a href="#S8.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 8.1. ‣ Control of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.1</span></a>, which is local in nature, extends to the case of partial desingularizations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S9.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 9.1</span></span><span id="S9.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S9.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S9.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{1,...,n\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{1,...,n\}</annotation></semantics></math>. We have the following controls:</span></p>
<ol id="S9.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S9.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(i)</span> 
<div id="S9.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S9.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k}}_{t}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})-\mho^{A_{k}}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k}}_{t})}=o(t_{k}),\text{ as $t_{k}\to 0$}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mi>α</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> as </mtext><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k}}_{t}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})-\mho^{A_{k}}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k}}_{t})}=o(t_{k}),\text{ as $t_{k}\to 0$},</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S9.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(ii)</span> 
<div id="S9.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S9.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D_{k}}_{t})}=o(t_{k}),\text{ as $t_{k}\to 0$}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_mathvariant_italic"> as </mtext><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D_{k}}_{t})}=o(t_{k}),\text{ as $t_{k}\to 0$},</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S9.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> and</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S9.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">(iii)</span> 
<div id="S9.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">at every point, the eigenvalues of the self-dual Weyl curvature of </span><math id="S9.I2.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S9.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> are arbitrarily close to those of </span><math id="S9.I2.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S9.I2.i3.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> at some corresponding point of </span><math id="S9.I2.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S9.I2.i3.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S9.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">We will prove this by induction on <math id="S9.SSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>.
When <math id="S9.SSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=0</annotation></semantics></math>, one has <math id="S9.SSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> and the result is clear.
Proceeding by induction, let us now assume that the Proposition holds for <math id="S9.SSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>⩽</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0\leqslant k\leqslant n-1</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text">To prove (<a href="#S9.I2.i1" title="item i ‣ Proposition 9.1. ‣ Controlling the approximate desingularizations ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">i</span></a>), notice that the control of</span></p>
<table id="S9.Ex62" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S9.Ex62.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}_{t}}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})-\mho^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k+1}}_{t})}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}_{t}}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})-\mho^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k+1}}_{t})}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S9.SSx2.p3.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p3.2.1" class="ltx_text">is exactly as in the proof of (<a href="#S8.E23" title="In Proposition 8.1. ‣ Control of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a>), as the argument is local, and therefore also applies to partial desingularizations; cf. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Proposition 5.13]</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">To prove (<a href="#S9.I2.i2" title="item ii ‣ Proposition 9.1. ‣ Controlling the approximate desingularizations ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">ii</span></a>), notice that, as in
Section <a href="#S8.SSx4" title="Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems and ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, we once again have</span></p>

<p id="S9.SSx2.p4.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text">for some <math id="S9.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, where the right-hand side is <math id="S9.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(t_{k+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(t_{k+1})</annotation></semantics></math> as <math id="S9.SSx2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k+1}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k+1}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
Indeed, this follows from (<a href="#S9.I2.i1" title="item i ‣ Proposition 9.1. ‣ Controlling the approximate desingularizations ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">i</span></a>) and <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, (88), Proposition 5.11]</cite>, the proof of which
does not require the existence of an Einstein desingularization, but instead holds for any </span><span id="S9.SSx2.p4.2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein-modulo-obstructions</span><span id="S9.SSx2.p4.2.3" class="ltx_text"> metric.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text">Finally, to prove (<a href="#S9.I2.i3" title="item iii ‣ Proposition 9.1. ‣ Controlling the approximate desingularizations ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">iii</span></a>), notice that the proof of Corollary <a href="#S8.Thmthm4" title="Corollary 8.4. ‣ Curvature of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a> also works in our present setting, both at and away from the orbifold singularities.
By the property for <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, the metric <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>, which plays the role of <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> in Section <a href="#S8.SSx4" title="Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems and ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8</span></a>, has self-dual Weyl curvature with eigenvalues arbitrarily close to those
of <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> at some corresponding. An extension of the proof of Corollary <a href="#S8.Thmthm4" title="Corollary 8.4. ‣ Curvature of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">8.4</span></a>, which is local in nature, then shows that the eigenvalues of <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}(g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v})</annotation></semantics></math> are arbitrarily close to
those of <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> at an appropriate point.
We then conclude, in exact analogy to (<a href="#S8.E24" title="In Proof-of-Concept Versions of Theorems and ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">24</span></a>), that</span></p>
<table id="S9.EGx13" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_eqnarray ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="S9.SSx2.p5.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx2.p5.2.1" class="ltx_text">where the right-hand side tends to zero as <math id="S9.SSx2.p5.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>

</section>
<section id="S9.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Conclusion of the proof</h3>

<div id="S9.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Bringing these ideas together, let us now assume</p>
<ul id="S9.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S9.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">that <math id="S9.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> is an orbifold with <math id="S9.I3.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> isolated singularities <math id="S9.I3.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1},...,p_{n}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1},...,p_{n}</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S9.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">that <math id="S9.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is Hermitian and Einstein, with <math id="S9.I3.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>;</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S9.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">that there is an admissible sequence <math id="S9.I3.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> with</p>
<table id="S9.Ex65" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
