</div></li>
<li id="S9.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">that no trees of singularities arise in this limiting process.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, then, up to taking a subsequence, for <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> large enough, there exist <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{i}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{i}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, along with naïve desingularizations <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> and parameters</p>
<table id="S9.Ex66" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S9.Ex66.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{i}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b_{1}})\times...\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{b_{n}})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msub><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{i}\in\mathfrak{O}(g_{b_{1}})\times...\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{b_{n}})\times\mathfrak{O}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S9.SSx3.p2.2" class="ltx_p">for which</p>
<ul id="S9.I4" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S9.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S9.I4.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g_{i}-g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g_{i}-g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{i}})}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S9.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S9.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S9.I4.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="g_{i}-g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\perp_{g^{D}_{t_{i}}}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msubsup><msub><mo>⟂</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}-g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}}\perp_{g^{D}_{t_{i}}}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{n}}_{t_{i},v_{i}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S9.SSx3.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Since our assumptions in particular imply that <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> has the expected topology, and all of the Ricci-flat ALE spaces arising from curvature concentration are Kähler,
our assumption that no trees of singularities arise
then implies <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, §7.1]</cite>
that, after passing to a subsequence and up to a diffeomorphism, <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}=\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{i},v_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}=\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{i},v_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> for one of the above <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{i},v_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{i},v_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In particular, <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is an Einstein metric
satisfying Wu’s criterion <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det\operatorname{W}^{+}(g_{i})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">det</mo><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det\operatorname{W}^{+}(g_{i})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, and it
therefore follows <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> that, for <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> large enough, the <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> are necessarily <span id="S9.SSx3.p2.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">conformally Kähler</span>. However, as previously noted, such metrics on a smooth <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> are actually
Kähler-Einstein unless <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> there is, up to isometries and rescalings, only one conformally-Kähler Einstein manifold on <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> thus now follow in the case where no trees of singularities arise.  <math id="S9.SSx3.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S9.SSx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Combining this with Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm3" title="Proposition 4.3. ‣ 4 Constraints on Diffeotype ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a>
now yields the following application:</p>
</div>
<div id="S9.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S9.Thmthm2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 9.2</span></span><span id="S9.Thmthm2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S9.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X^{4},g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>X</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X^{4},g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> be a Kähler-Einstein orbifold with at least one singular point. If <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>, and if <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is the Gromov-Hausdorff limit of an
admissible sequence <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> of smooth <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Einstein <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds, then <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(X)=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(X)=4</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S9.Thmthm2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\approx{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#5\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>≈</mo><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\approx{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#5\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S9.SSx3.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S9.SSx3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.SSx3.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S9.SSx3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">When <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is Kähler-Einstein,
Proposition <a href="#S4.Thmthm3" title="Proposition 4.3. ‣ 4 Constraints on Diffeotype ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.3</span></a> tells us that each singularity of <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> is modeled on <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}^{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℂ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>ℤ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}^{2}/{\mathbb{Z}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and this in particular
excludes the formation of bubble-trees. The above
argument therefore shows that the Einstein <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> must be Hermitian
for all sufficiently large <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. However, classification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite> tells us
that, up to isometry and rescalings, there is at most one <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Hermitian, Einstein metric on the underlying smooth <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> of a complex surface with <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}\geq 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo>≥</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}\geq 5</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(X)\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>, singularities can therefore
only form in the limit
when <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{1}^{2}(M)=c_{1}^{2}(X)=4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>c</mi><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{1}^{2}(M)=c_{1}^{2}(X)=4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is
diffeomorphic to <math id="S9.SSx3.p4.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#5\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#5\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S10" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">10 </span>The General Case</h2>

<div id="S10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we deal with trees of singularities by further refining our notion of approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric.
In fact, our proof of Proposition <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Proposition 2.2. ‣ 2 Singularities of Type T ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> already depended on the reason why it is possible to handle trees of Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metrics: when glued together in the expected manner, they can always
be approximated by a <span id="S10.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">single</span> Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metric <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>. The essence of what we will now do amounts to a controlled, quantitative implementation of this observation. While
there are more elementary ways of carrying this out for the Gibbons-Hawking gravitational instantons, our proof will be geared to handle the general case.</p>
</div>
<section id="S10.SS0.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Asymptotics of the building blocks</h4>

<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We will now consider:</p>
<ul id="S10.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N_{1},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N_{1},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})</annotation></semantics></math> a Ricci-flat ALE orbifold with a singularity at <math id="S10.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N_{2},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N_{2},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}})</annotation></semantics></math> glued at scale <math id="S10.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> at a remaining singular point <math id="S10.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S10.I1.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N_{1},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>N</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N_{1},\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We have the following expansions of the different metrics: for any <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\leqslant 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\leqslant 4</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<ul id="S10.I2" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">at its singular point <math id="S10.I2.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>: <math id="S10.I2.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}}={\boldsymbol{\delta}}+\mathfrak{H}_{2}+\mathfrak{H}_{3}+\mathfrak{H}_{4}+...+\mathfrak{H}_{l}+\mathsf{O}(\rho_{b_{1}}^{l+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝜹</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}}={\boldsymbol{\delta}}+\mathfrak{H}_{2}+\mathfrak{H}_{3}+\mathfrak{H}_{4}+...+\mathfrak{H}_{l}+\mathsf{O}(\rho_{b_{1}}^{l+1})</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">at its infinity: <math id="S10.I2.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}={\boldsymbol{\delta}}+\mathfrak{H}^{4}+...+\mathfrak{H}^{l}+\mathsf{O}(\rho_{b_{2}}^{l+1})." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝜹</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>l</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ρ</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}={\boldsymbol{\delta}}+\mathfrak{H}^{4}+...+\mathfrak{H}^{l}+\mathsf{O}(\rho_{b_{2}}^{l+1}).</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">In particular, developing the equations <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(g_{b_{1}})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(g_{b_{1}})=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(g_{b_{2}})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(g_{b_{2}})=0</annotation></semantics></math> according to powers of <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{b_{1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{b_{1}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{b_{2}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{b_{2}}</annotation></semantics></math> the above tensors satisfy equalities:</p>
<ul id="S10.I3" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I3.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I3.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}\mathfrak{H}_{i}+Q^{[i],+}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}_{2},\mathfrak{H}_{3},...,\mathfrak{H}_{i-1})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>𝜹</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}\mathfrak{H}_{i}+Q^{[i],+}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}_{2},\mathfrak{H}_{3},...,\mathfrak{H}_{i-1})=0</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I3.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I3.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I3.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}\mathfrak{H}^{j}+Q^{[j],-}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}^{4},\mathfrak{H}^{5},...,\mathfrak{H}^{j-1})=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>𝜹</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}\mathfrak{H}^{j}+Q^{[j],-}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}^{4},\mathfrak{H}^{5},...,\mathfrak{H}^{j-1})=0</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{[j],\pm}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>𝜹</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">±</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{[j],\pm}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}</annotation></semantics></math> are specific finite sums of multilinear operations on the tensors and their two first derivatives. The key point is that <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{[i],+}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}_{2},\mathfrak{H}_{3},\ldots,\mathfrak{H}_{i-1})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{i-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>𝜹</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">+</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϱ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{[i],+}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}_{2},\mathfrak{H}_{3},\ldots,\mathfrak{H}_{i-1})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{i-2})</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q^{[j],-}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}^{4},\mathfrak{H}^{5},\ldots,\mathfrak{H}^{j-1})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{-j-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>Q</mi><mi>𝜹</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>5</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>ϱ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q^{[j],-}_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}(\mathfrak{H}^{4},\mathfrak{H}^{5},\ldots,\mathfrak{H}^{j-1})=\mathsf{O}(\varrho^{-j-2})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10.SS0.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Approximations of
Ricci-flat Kähler metrics</h4>

<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">When <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{b}=(v_{b_{1}},t_{2},v_{b_{2}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{b}=(v_{b_{1}},t_{2},v_{b_{2}})</annotation></semantics></math> is sufficiently small, we will use <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B}_{v_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>B</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B}_{v_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> to denote
the naïve gluing <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}}\#_{p_{1},t_{2}}\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>#</mi><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}}\#_{p_{1},t_{2}}\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}</annotation></semantics></math> and let <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> be the associated extension of <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}</annotation></semantics></math> of Definition <a href="#Thmdefn7" title="Definition 7 (Function ϱ_𝐷 on a naïve desingularization). ‣ Gluing of ALE spaces to orbifold singularities. ‣ 7 Desingularizing Einstein Orbifolds ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>. By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 6.2]</cite>, there is a unique Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metric <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b}}</annotation></semantics></math> that, for some <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, satisfies</p>
<ol id="S10.I4" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S10.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S10.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I4.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g^{B}_{v_{b}}}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})=0," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>B</mi></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g^{B}_{v_{b}}}(\bar{g}_{v_{b}})=0,</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S10.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I4.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B}_{v_{b}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}}\leqslant\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>B</mi></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em">⩽</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B}_{v_{b}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}}\leqslant\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S10.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I4.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B}_{v_{b}}\perp_{L^{2}(g_{b})}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>B</mi></msubsup><msub><mo>⟂</mo><mrow><msup><mi>L</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B}_{v_{b}}\perp_{L^{2}(g_{b})}\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mi>B</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})</annotation></semantics></math> is defined in Definition <a href="#Thmdefn16" title="Definition 16 (𝐶^{2,𝛼}_{𝛽,∗∗} norm on an ALE orbifold). ‣ Decoupling norms. ‣ Appendix A Function Spaces ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">16</span></a> below.
We emphasize that this construction reaches <span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">all</span> nearby Ricci-flat ALE metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The results of <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 6.2]</cite> tell us that any Einstein-modulo-obstructions perturbation of a tree of Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metrics is in fact a Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metric. For any <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, this metric can then be approximated by a naïve gluing:</p>
<table id="S10.E27" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B,[l]}_{v_{b}}:=\Big(\overline{g}_{v_{b_{1}}}+\sum_{j=4}^{l}t_{2}^{\frac{j}{2}}h^{j}\Big)\#_{p_{1},t_{2}}\Big(\overline{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}+\sum_{i=2}^{l}t_{2}^{\frac{i}{2}}h_{i}\Big),</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(27)</span></td></tr></tbody>

<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where for <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i,j\leqslant 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i,j\leqslant 4</annotation></semantics></math>, one defines the <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h^{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>h</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h^{j}</annotation></semantics></math> as in (<a href="#S8.E18" title="In item 1 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">18</span></a>), (<a href="#S8.E19" title="In item 2 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">19</span></a>), (<a href="#S8.E21" title="In item 4 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">21</span></a>) where all of the obstructions <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mho_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mho_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{w}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐰</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation Following (<a href="#S8.E22" title="In item 5 ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">22</span></a>), we now solve iteratively for <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i,j\geqslant 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>⩾</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i,j\geqslant 4</annotation></semantics></math> by applying the following two steps:</p>

<p id="S10.I5.i1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">Since the gluing is unobstructed by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 6.2]</cite>, one then shows iteratively that the element of <math id="S10.I5.i1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b_{1}}})</annotation></semantics></math> vanishes, and <math id="S10.I5.i1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" <p id="S10.I5.i2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S10.I5.i2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}^{[j],+}" display="inline" encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{H}_{j}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.I5.i2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\leqslant j" display="inline" </div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The point is that there are <span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">no obstructions</span> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 6.2]</cite> which lets us estimate the metrics directly without having to approximate obstructions. Explicit computations generalizing slightly those of Proposition <a href="#S8.E23" title="In Proposition 8.1. ‣ Control of the approximate solutions ‣ 8 Simplest Case of the Proof ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">23</span></a> (see also <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>, Sections 2 and 3]</cite>) lead to the following result.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 10.1</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\geqslant 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩾</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\geqslant 4</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\beta&lt;\frac{1}{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>β</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\beta&lt;\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>, there is <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> independent of <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> so that we have the control</span></p>

<p id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">and consequently, by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, (5.15), Lemma 5.19]</cite>, we therefore have</span></p>
<table id="S10.Ex75" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex75.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B,[l]}_{v_{b}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})}\leqslant C^{\prime}t_{2}^{\frac{l+1-\beta}{4}}=o(t_{2}^{\frac{l}{4}})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>l</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></msubsup><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>B</mi></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em">⩽</mo><msup><mi>C</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mrow><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mi>o</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mn>2</mn><mfrac><mi>l</mi><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\bar{g}_{v_{b}}-g^{B,[l]}_{v_{b}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}(g^{B}_{v_{b}})}\leqslant C^{\prime}t_{2}^{\frac{l+1-\beta}{4}}=o(t_{2}^{\frac{l}{4}})</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.3" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">for some <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{\prime}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{\prime}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> independent of <math id="S10.Thmthm1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="v_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">v_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In particular, considering <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\geqslant 9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩾</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\geqslant 9</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have the following controls.</p>
</div>

<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">We finish this section by an estimate of the variations at infinity of a tree of singularities with respect to the size of the bubbles attached to it.</p>
<ul id="S10.I7" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I7.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I7.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I7.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">for <math id="S10.I7.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\{0,...,k+1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\{0,...,k+1\}</annotation></semantics></math>, Ricci-flat Kähler <math id="S10.I7.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{l}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>l</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{l}}</annotation></semantics></math> that can be glued as a tree of singularities according to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Section 4.3]</cite></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I7.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span>

<p id="S10.I7.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I7.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" enough <math id="S10.I7.i2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{l}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation <p id="S10.I7.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I7.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="S10.I7.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>) the Ricci-flat Kähler ALE perturbation of <math id="S10.I7.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="S10.I7.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>),</p>

<div id="S10.Thmthm3" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 10.3</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm3.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{B_{k}}\gg\sqrt{T_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><mo>≫</mo><msqrt><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{B_{k}}\gg\sqrt{T_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have, for any <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\mathbf{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>𝐍</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\mathbf{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{l}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{l}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> depending only on <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S10.E30" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.E30.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho^{l}_{B_{k}}|\nabla^{l}(\bar{g}_{B_{k}}-\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}})|\leqslant C_{l}T_{k+1}^{2}r_{B_{k}}^{-4}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msup><mo>∇</mo><mi>l</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho^{l}_{B_{k}}|\nabla^{l}(\bar{g}_{B_{k}}-\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}})|\leqslant C_{l}T_{k+1}^{2}r_{B_{k}}^{-4}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(30)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">More precisely, there is a converging expansion</span></p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
