</table>
<p id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">with <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathfrak{K}^{j}|\leqslant C_{j}^{\prime}T_{k+1}^{2}\varrho^{-j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>𝔎</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ϱ</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathfrak{K}^{j}|\leqslant C_{j}^{\prime}T_{k+1}^{2}\varrho^{-j}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{j}^{\prime}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{j}^{\prime}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> independent of <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S10.Thmthm3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Sketch of proof.</h6>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.1.1" class="ltx_text">The result can be easily obtained for the Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metrics asymptotic to <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}/\Gamma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}/\Gamma</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma\subset SU(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>U</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma\subset SU(2)</annotation></semantics></math> cyclic. Indeed, they are Gibbons-Hawking’s gravitational instantons which are </span><span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">explicitly</span><span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p6.1.3" class="ltx_text"> given in coordinates <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p7.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SS0.SSSx2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text">For the general case, one can combine the resolution of singularities described in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, Proposition 3.10]</cite> together with the description of the asymptotic expansion of the <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, Proposition 3.14]</cite> (see also <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, Theorem 2.1]</cite>).
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10.SSx1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Approximate metrics with trees of singularities</h3>

<div id="S10.SSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now explain how to deal with trees of singularities.</p>
</div>
<section id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">Setting up the iterative construction</h4>

<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this section, we consider <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>, a conformally Kähler Einstein orbifold with scalar curvature <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>12</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">12</annotation></semantics></math> with multiple singularities of general type. We then consider a naïve desingularization of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> at all of its singularities by trees of singularities which we will denote <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>D</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">We will order our desingularizations according to their <span id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">depth</span>, that is the size of the bubbles glued.</p>
<ol id="S10.I8" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S10.I8.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S10.I8.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I8.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">we start with <math id="S10.I8.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}:=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}:=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}:=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mn>0</mn></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>o</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{0}}_{t,v}:=g^{A_{0}}_{t,v}:=\hat{g}^{0}_{t,v}:=\bar{g}_{v_{o}}</annotation></semantics></math> as before, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I8.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S10.I8.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I8.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">given <math id="S10.I8.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the next largest scale <math id="S10.I8.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> at which to glue a Ricci-flat ALE metric <math id="S10.I8.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{{v_{k+1}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{{v_{k+1}}}</annotation></semantics></math> to a remaining singular point <math id="S10.I8.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S10.Ex80" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex80.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k+1}}_{t,v}:=g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}\;\#_{p_{k+1},T_{k}^{2}t_{k+1}}\;\bar{g}_{v_{k+1}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>#</mi><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k+1}}_{t,v}:=g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}\;\#_{p_{k+1},T_{k}^{2}t_{k+1}}\;\bar{g}_{v_{k+1}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The rest of the argument mainly consists in carefully constructing approximations <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> in order to control the Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and their curvature. We will eventually reach the total Einstein-modulo-obstructions desingularization and be able to control its curvature.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm4" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 10.4</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm4.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each <math id="S10.Thmthm4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\{1,...,n\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\{1,...,n\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have:</span></p>
<ol id="S10.I9" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S10.I9.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S10.I9.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">at every point, the eignenvalues of the self-dual curvature </span><math id="S10.I9.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> of </span><math id="S10.I9.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> differ form the eigenvalues of </span><math id="S10.I9.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}(g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}(g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">,
at a suitable point of </span><math id="S10.I9.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, by only an
error that uniformly tends to zero as </span><math id="S10.I9.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to(0,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to(0,0)</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i1.p1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">;</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I9.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S10.I9.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I9.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I9.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}=o(T_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}=o(T_{k})</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">, and there is </span><math id="S10.I9.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> such that for any </span><math id="S10.I9.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\{0,1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\{0,1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math><span id="S10.I9.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">; and</span></p>
<table id="S10.E31" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.E31.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\nabla^{l}(\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{D_{k}})|\leqslant Cr_{D_{k}}^{2}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msup><mo>∇</mo><mi>l</mi></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>2</mn></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\nabla^{l}(\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}-g^{D_{k}})|\leqslant Cr_{D_{k}}^{2}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(31)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection">The iterative step</h4>

<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">If we have previously defined <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}}_{t,v})</annotation></semantics></math> in a suitable manner, we may then define <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> so as to control <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">If the next considered singular point <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> is a singular point of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, then we define <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k+1}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and obtain a control of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and its curvature exactly as in Section <a href="#S9" title="9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>. Here, we will therefore consider the remaining case where the singular point <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> belongs to another Ricci-flat ALE metric of the tree of singularities.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Note.</span>
In order to simplify our notation in the remainder of the argument, we will drop (when not necessary) the <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)</annotation></semantics></math>-dependence of our tensors and in particular denote <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{i}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{i}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{v_{b_{i}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{v_{b_{i}}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
 <span class="ltx_rule" style="width:5.0pt;height:10.0pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span> 
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Assume that:</p>
<ul id="S10.I10" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I10.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I10.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I10.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I10.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.I10.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> defined from the previous steps, satisfy:</p>
<table id="S10.E32" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.E32.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k}}}(\hat{g}^{k})=\mathfrak{w}_{0}+\mathfrak{w}_{2}+\mathsf{O}(T_{k}r_{b_{k}}^{3})\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mn>3</mn></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k}}}(\hat{g}^{k})=\mathfrak{w}_{0}+\mathfrak{w}_{2}+\mathsf{O}(T_{k}r_{b_{k}}^{3})\in\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(32)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S10.I10.i1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with <math id="S10.I10.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathfrak{w}_{l}|\leqslant C_{l}T_{k}r_{b_{k}}^{l}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>l</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathfrak{w}_{l}|\leqslant C_{l}T_{k}r_{b_{k}}^{l}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.I10.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{l}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{l}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I10.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I10.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I10.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I10.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k+1}}=g^{D_{k}}\;\#_{p_{k+1},T_{k}^{2}t_{k+1}}\;g_{{b_{k+1}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>#</mi><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi><mn>2</mn></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k+1}}=g^{D_{k}}\;\#_{p_{k+1},T_{k}^{2}t_{k+1}}\;g_{{b_{k+1}}}</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="S10.I10.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{{b_{k+1}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{{b_{k+1}}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a Ricci-flat ALE metric with a remaining singular point <math id="S10.I10.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I10.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I10.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I10.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I10.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> the Einstein-modulo-obstructions perturbation of <math id="S10.I10.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k+1}}=g^{D_{k+1}}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k+1}}=g^{D_{k+1}}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> transversely to <math id="S10.I10.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\mathfrak{O}}(g^{A_{k}})</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Our goal will now be to obtain curvature estimates for <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> using the construction of an approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric. We will in particular show that the above properties stay true by iteration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For this we will also use the following metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S10.I11" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S10.I11.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I11.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I11.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I11.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the naïve gluing of the tree of singularity at which <math id="S10.I11.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> is glued in <math id="S10.I11.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I11.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I11.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I11.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I11.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the naïve gluing of the tree of singularity at which <math id="S10.I11.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> is glued in <math id="S10.I11.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, but <span id="S10.I11.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">without</span> <math id="S10.I11.i2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{b_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{b_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S10.I11.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S10.I11.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I11.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S10.I11.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{B_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="S10.I11.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>) the Ricci-flat Kähler ALE perturbation of <math id="S10.I11.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> (resp. <math id="S10.I11.i3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">The rest of the section consists in constructing a suitable approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math> controlling <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o(T_{k+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o(T_{k+1})</annotation></semantics></math> in order to compensate the <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho_{D}^{-2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho_{D}^{-2}</annotation></semantics></math> term of our function space. For this, we will leverage the fact that both <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}_{B_{k}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}_{B_{k}}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy <span id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">exact</span> equations in order to rule out errors in powers of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> alone or in powers of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> alone. The following key technical lemma follows from the expansion of Ricci curvature at a metric <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> in the (small) direction <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="S10.Ex81" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex81.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r(g+h)=r(g)+(g+h)^{-1}*{\mathcal{R}}(g)+(g+h)^{-2}*\nabla^{2}h+(g+h)^{-3}*\nabla h*\nabla h," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.222em">∗</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.222em">∗</mo><mrow><msup><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo rspace="0.222em">∗</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∗</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r(g+h)=r(g)+(g+h)^{-1}*{\mathcal{R}}(g)+(g+h)^{-2}*\nabla^{2}h+(g+h)^{-3}*\nabla h*\nabla h,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="*" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∗</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">*</annotation></semantics></math> corresponds to contractions of tensors.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm5" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 10.5</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm5.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> be an Einstein metric on an open set <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U\subset\mathbb{R}^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>U</mi><mo>⊂</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U\subset\mathbb{R}^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\nabla^{l}_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}(g-{\boldsymbol{\delta}})|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}&lt;\frac{1}{100}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∇</mo><mi>𝛅</mi><mi>l</mi></msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>𝛅</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>𝛅</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>100</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\nabla^{l}_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}(g-{\boldsymbol{\delta}})|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}&lt;\frac{1}{100}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\leqslant L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mi>L</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\leqslant L</annotation></semantics></math>. Assume that there exist <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> small enough in <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{L}(U,{\boldsymbol{\delta}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>C</mi><mi>L</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>U</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>𝛅</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{L}(U,{\boldsymbol{\delta}})</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathscr{F}_{g}(g+h_{i})=w_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathscr{F}_{g}(g+h_{i})=w_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,2\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,2\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Then, we have the following control: there exists a <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{L}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{L}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, independent of <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g,h_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g,h_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, such that, for <math id="S10.Thmthm5.p2.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="l\in\{0,...,\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\{0,...,\}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S10.Ex82" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark.</span>
The assumption on <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> always holds in suitably rescaled harmonic coordinates, whether our space is a manifold or an orbifold; cf. e.g. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>.
 <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\diamondsuit" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">♢</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\diamondsuit</annotation></semantics></math> 
<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Near the singular point <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>p</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math>, we have the following expansions of the relevant metrics:</p>

<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathfrak{K}_{i}|\leqslant T_{k}r_{B_{k}}^{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>𝔎</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mi>i</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathfrak{K}_{i}|\leqslant T_{k}r_{B_{k}}^{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
In particular, by the equation satisfied by <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mi>k</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}_{t,v}</annotation></semantics></math> and (<a href="#S10.E32" title="In 1st item ‣ The iterative step ‣ Approximate metrics with trees of singularities ‣ 10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">32</span></a>), the above tensors satisfy the following equalities:</p>

<p id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Extending the results of Section <a href="#S8.SSx1.SSSx2" title="Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions metrics ‣ Approximate Einstein-modulo-obstructions extending the above ones: given the <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>h</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> of (<a href="#S10.E29" title="In item 2 ‣ Approximations of Ricci-flat Kähler metrics ‣ 10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">29</span></a>), and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> extensions of <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>𝔴</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{w}_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S10.SSx1.SSSx2.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{w}_{2}" display="inline" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>𝔒</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><msub><mi>v</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></msub></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}k_{4}+Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}(k_{0},h_{4})+Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}(h_{2},h_{2})+Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}(k_{0},h_{2},h_{2})+Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}(k_{0},k_{2},h_{2})+Q_{\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}}}(k_{0},k_{2},k_{2})-\Lambda(h_{2}+k_{2})-w_{2}=\mho_{4}\in\mathfrak{O}(\bar{g}_{v_{b_{2}}})</annotation></semantics></math>.

<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>

<section id="S10.SSx2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Approximate metrics with trees of singularities</h3>

<div id="S10.SSx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We now control how close we are to the actual Einstein-modulo-obstructions metric. This proves the last point of Proposition <a href="#S10.Thmthm4" title="Proposition 10.4. ‣ Setting up the iterative construction ‣ Approximate metrics with trees of singularities ‣ 10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm6" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 10.6</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm6.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">We have the following control:</span></p>
<table id="S10.Ex86" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex86.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}}(g^{A_{k+1}})-\mho^{A_{k+1}}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k+1}})}\leqslant o(T_{k+1})." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">ℱ</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">℧</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>D</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mi>α</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>⩽</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\mathscr{F}_{g^{D_{k+1}}}(g^{A_{k+1}})-\mho^{A_{k+1}}\|_{\varrho_{D}^{-2}C^{\alpha}_{\beta}(g^{D_{k+1}})}\leqslant o(T_{k+1}).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Thus, by <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>, Proposition 5.11]</cite>, we have
<math id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k+1}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D_{k+1}})}=o(T_{k+1})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|\hat{g}^{k+1}_{t,v}-g^{A_{k+1}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D_{k+1}})}=o(T_{k+1})</annotation></semantics></math>. In particular, since <math id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r_{D_{k+1}}\geqslant T_{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo>⩾</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r_{D_{k+1}}\geqslant T_{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> there is <math id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> such that for any <math id="S10.Thmthm6.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\in\{0,1,2,3\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\in\{0,1,2,3\}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S10.Ex87" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<div id="S10.SSx2.1" class="ltx_proof">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_font_italic ltx_title_proof">Proof.</h6>
<div id="S10.SSx2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SSx2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text">There are three regions to consider, and we will control our operator on each of them.</span></p>

and (<a href="#S10.E31" title="In item 2 ‣ Proposition 10.4. ‣ Setting up the iterative construction ‣ Approximate metrics with trees of singularities ‣ 10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">31</span></a>) we find:</p>

<p id="S10.I14.i3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here, the error comes from multilinear terms involving the following tensors such that for all <math id="S10.I14.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="l\leqslant 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>⩽</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">l\leqslant 3</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists <math id="S10.I14.i3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C_{l}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mi>l</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C_{l}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> so that</p>

</div></li>
<li id="S10.I14.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S10.I14.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.I14.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Lastly, in the cut-off region <math id="S10.I14.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}t_{k+1}^{\frac{2}{9}}&lt;r_{D_{k+1}}&lt;2T_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}t_{k+1}^{\frac{2}{9}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></msubsup></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>D</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>T</mi><mi>k</mi><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}t_{k+1}^{\frac{2}{9}}&lt;r_{D_{k+1}}&lt;2T_{k}^{\frac{1}{2}}t_{k+1}^{\frac{2}{9}}</annotation></semantics></math>, the difference of the metrics is in:</p>
