</div>
<div id="S10.SSx2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.SSx2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text">Putting all of this together, we consequently obtain the stated estimate by gluing at scale <math id="S10.SSx2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t_{k+1}^{\frac{1}{5}}\ll r_{b_{k+1}}\ll t_{k+1}^{\frac{1}{4}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></msubsup><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>r</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msub><mo>≪</mo><msubsup><mi>t</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t_{k+1}^{\frac{1}{5}}\ll r_{b_{k+1}}\ll t_{k+1}^{\frac{1}{4}}</annotation></semantics></math>, which is satisfied by the scale of gluing chosen in the definition of <math id="S10.SSx2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{A_{k+1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>A</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{A_{k+1}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
∎</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Mimicking the proof of the third point of Proposition <a href="#S9.Thmthm1" title="Proposition 9.1. ‣ Controlling the approximate desingularizations ‣ 9 Without Trees of Singularities ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9.1</span></a> now yields the following result.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.Thmthm7" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_cor">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S10.Thmthm7.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Corollary 10.7</span></span><span id="S10.Thmthm7.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="S10.Thmthm7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">If the eigenvalues of the self-dual Weyl curvature <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>k</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k}</annotation></semantics></math> are, are uniformly close to those of <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> at some corresponding point of <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>,
then the eigenvalues of the self-dual Weyl curvature <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{k+1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{k+1}</annotation></semantics></math> also have this property, with an error that uniformly tends to zero as <math id="S10.Thmthm7.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(t,v)\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(t,v)\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10.SSx3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection">Conclusion of the proof</h3>

<div id="S10.SSx3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let us now assume that the <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Einstein orbifold <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> is
conformally Kähler, and that there is
an admissible sequence <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> with</p>
<table id="S10.Ex93" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex93.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{GH}\Big((M,g_{i}),(X,g_{\infty})\Big)\to 0." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo maxsize="1.600em" minsize="1.600em">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{GH}\Big((M,g_{i}),(X,g_{\infty})\Big)\to 0.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S10.SSx3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>, after passing to a subsequence indexed by <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, and for sufficiently large <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, there thus exist naïve desingularizations
<math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math> such that <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|g_{j}-g^{D}_{t_{j}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{j}})}\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|g_{j}-g^{D}_{t_{j}}\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}(g^{D}_{t_{j}})}\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>, possibly with the involvement of
trees of singularities.
After perhaps refining our subsequence, the associated gluing scales <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{k,j}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{k,j}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> in the tree can then be ordered such that, for all <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="S10.Ex94" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S10.Ex94.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{1,j}\leqslant T_{2,j}\leqslant...\leqslant T_{n,j}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>⩽</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>⩽</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{1,j}\leqslant T_{2,j}\leqslant...\leqslant T_{n,j}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S10.SSx3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">By <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>, <a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, each <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> is then isometric to some such <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{j},v_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{g}^{n}_{t_{j},v_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S10.SSx3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">However, the two lowest eigenvalues of <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> are everywhere negative and equal
for the conformally Kähler <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> Einstein orbifold metric <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math>. By Corollary <a href="#S10.Thmthm7" title="Corollary 10.7. ‣ Approximate metrics with trees of singularities ‣ 10 The General Case ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10.7</span></a>,
it therefore follows, for <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>, that the two lowest eigenvalues of the self-dual Weyl curvatures <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> of our Einstein metrics <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>
are therefore everywhere negative. Since <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W^{+}\in\End(\Lambda^{+})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi>End</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W^{+}\in\End(\Lambda^{+})</annotation></semantics></math> is trace-free, this means that these <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> must have <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\det(W^{+})&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo rspace="0em">det</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\det(W^{+})&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>
everywhere. Thus, all but a finite number of the Einstein metrics <math id="S10.SSx3.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> must actually satisfy Wu’s criterion (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">It is therefore a formal consequence that
all but a finite number of the original <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> must also satisfy (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). Indeed, there would otherwise be a subsequence <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}\subset\{g_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mo>⊂</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}\subset\{g_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> consisting of Einstein metrics that <span id="S10.SSx3.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">do not</span> satisfy (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>). But since the <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}</annotation></semantics></math> would still be an admissible sequence converging
to <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>, the above argument would then demonstrate that (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>) must hold for an infinite number of the <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msup><mi>j</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{g_{j^{\prime}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and this is of course
a contradiction.
This shows that, for all <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math>, the original <math id="S10.SSx3.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{g_{i}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{g_{i}\}</annotation></semantics></math> must actually satisfy (<a href="#S6.E1" title="In 6 The Role of Wu’s Criterion ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>), and must therefore <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite> be conformally Kähler.</p>
</div>
<div id="S10.SSx3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.SSx3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The classification <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, Theorem A]</cite> of conformally Kähler, Einstein metrics on smooth, compact <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds therefore tells us that these <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> must actually
be Kähler-Einstein unless <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is either <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#2\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℙ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>#</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>ℂ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ℙ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="true">¯</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}_{2}\#2\overline{{\mathbb{C}\mathbb{P}}}_{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, equipped with a constant multiple of the
Page metric or the Chen-LeBrun-Weber metric, respectively.
Since these exceptional metrics are also, up to isometry and rescaling, the <span id="S10.SSx3.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">only</span> conformally Kähler, Einstein metrics on
these exceptional manifolds, the <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g_{i})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> must in fact be Kähler-Einstein for <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\gg 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>≫</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\gg 0</annotation></semantics></math> if we assume that <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math>
either has an orbifold singularity, or is itself Kähler-Einstein. Theorems <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a> and <a href="#Thmmain2" title="Theorem B. ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Desingularizations of ConformallyKähler, Einstein Orbifolds" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a> thus now follow, as promised.
 <math id="S10.SSx3.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Box" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">□</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Box</annotation></semantics></math></p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a tensor <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, a point <math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> and a Riemannian manifold <math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g)</annotation></semantics></math>. The Hölder seminorm is defined as</p>

<div id="A1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For orbifolds, we consider a norm which is bounded for tensors decaying at the singular points.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn12" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn12.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 12</span></span><span id="Thmdefn12.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Weighted Hölder norms on an orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn12.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn12.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn12.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> an orbifold. Then, for any tensor <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmdefn12.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math>, we define</span></p>

</div>
<div id="A1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For ALE manifolds, we will consider a norm which is bounded for tensors decaying at infinity.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn13" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn13.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 13</span></span><span id="Thmdefn13.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Weighted Hölder norms on an ALE orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn13.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn13.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn13.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn13.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> be an ALE manifold. Then, for any tensor <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmdefn13.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, we define</span></p>

<p id="A1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">on <math id="A1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> ,
where <math id="A1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon_{X^{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msup><mi>X</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon_{X^{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> equals <math id="A1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> when <math id="A1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t}=g_{\infty}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t}=g_{\infty}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon_{N_{j}^{t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msubsup><mi>N</mi><mi>j</mi><mi>t</mi></msubsup></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon_{N_{j}^{t}}</annotation></semantics></math> equals <math id="A1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> where <math id="A1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{D}_{t}=t_{j}g_{b_{j}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>g</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>D</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>t</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><msub><mi>b</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{D}_{t}=t_{j}g_{b_{j}}</annotation></semantics></math> (see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>), we can define a global norm.</p>

<div id="Thmdefn14" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn14.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 14</span></span><span id="Thmdefn14.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Weighted Hölder norm on a naïve desingularization)<span id="Thmdefn14.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn14.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn14.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn14.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn14.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\in\mathbb{R}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\in\mathbb{R}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn14.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k\in\mathbb{N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>ℕ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k\in\mathbb{N}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="Thmdefn14.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\alpha&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\alpha&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math>. </div>
<div id="Thmdefn15" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn15.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 15</span></span><span id="Thmdefn15.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="Thmdefn15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}</annotation></semantics></math>-norm on <math id="Thmdefn15.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors)<span id="Thmdefn15.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn15.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn15.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn15.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> be a <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor on <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{D})</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math>. We define its <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}</annotation></semantics></math>-norm by</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex100" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex100.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|h\|_{C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}:=\inf_{h_{*},\mathfrak{H}_{k}}\|h_{*}\|_{C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta}}+\sum_{k}|\mathfrak{H}_{k}|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">inf</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></munder><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mi>k</mi></munder><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>𝜹</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h\|_{C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}:=\inf_{h_{*},\mathfrak{H}_{k}}\|h_{*}\|_{C^{k,\alpha}_{\beta}}+\sum_{k}|\mathfrak{H}_{k}|_{{\boldsymbol{\delta}}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmdefn15.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn15.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">where the infimum is taken on the <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(h_{*},(\mathfrak{H}_{k})_{k})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(h_{*},(\mathfrak{H}_{k})_{k})</annotation></semantics></math> satisfying <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=h_{*}+\sum_{k}\Upsilon_{A_{k}(t,\epsilon_{0})}\mathfrak{H}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=h_{*}+\sum_{k}\Upsilon_{A_{k}(t,\epsilon_{0})}\mathfrak{H}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g^{D})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mi>D</mi></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g^{D})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=h_{*}+\sum_{k}\Upsilon_{B_{k}(\epsilon_{0})}\mathfrak{H}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>h</mi><mo>∗</mo></msub><mo rspace="0.055em">+</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=h_{*}+\sum_{k}\Upsilon_{B_{k}(\epsilon_{0})}\mathfrak{H}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(X,g_{\infty})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">∞</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(X,g_{\infty})</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math>, where each <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathfrak{H}_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ℌ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathfrak{H}_{k}</annotation></semantics></math> is some constant and trace-free symmetric <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensors on <math id="Thmdefn15.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma_{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>/</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{R}^{4}/\penalty\Gamma_{k}</annotation></semantics></math>.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, we also introduce a function space that is particularly well-suited to Ricci-flat ALE spaces; cf. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, Definition 5.18]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmdefn16" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_defn">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefn16.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 16</span></span><span id="Thmdefn16.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(<math id="Thmdefn16.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}</annotation></semantics></math> norm on an ALE orbifold)<span id="Thmdefn16.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefn16.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefn16.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefn16.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(N,g_{b})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>N</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(N,g_{b})</annotation></semantics></math> be an ALE orbifold, let <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> be a <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-tensor on <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math>, and assume that <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h=\mathfrak{H}^{4}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-4-\beta})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>𝖮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h=\mathfrak{H}^{4}+\mathsf{O}(\varrho_{b}^{-4-\beta})</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. For <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, a cut-off function supported in <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N-K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N-K</annotation></semantics></math>.
We define the <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m9" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}</annotation></semantics></math>-norm of <math id="Thmdefn16.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> as:</span></p>
<table id="A1.Ex101" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.Ex101.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\|h\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}}:=\sup\varrho_{b}^{4}|\mathfrak{H}^{4}|_{g_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}+\big\|(1+\varrho_{b})^{4}(h-\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}^{4})\big\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><mi>h</mi><msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∗</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow></msub></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em" rspace="0.1389em">:=</mo><mo lspace="0.1389em" movablelimits="false" rspace="0.167em">sup</mo><msubsup><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi><mn>4</mn></msubsup><mo fence="false" rspace="0.167em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><msub><mo fence="false" stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi>𝜹</mi></msub></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">+</mo><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>4</mn></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>h</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msup><mi>ℌ</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em" mathsize="1.200em" rspace="0.0835em">∥</mo><msubsup><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0em">,</mo><mo lspace="0em">∗</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></msubsup></msub><mo lspace="0.0835em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|h\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,**}}:=\sup\varrho_{b}^{4}|\mathfrak{H}^{4}|_{g_{\boldsymbol{\delta}}}+\big\|(1+\varrho_{b})^{4}(h-\Upsilon\mathfrak{H}^{4})\big\|_{C^{2,\alpha}_{\beta,*}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Note that this definition actually corrects a minor error in <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite> that is fortunately harmless in most contexts. For a detailed
discussion of this point, see <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">23</a>, Remark A.12]</cite> concerning Ricci-flat Kähler ALE metrics.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS0.SSSx1.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Acknowledgments.</span> The authors would like to thank the Simons Center for Geometry and Physics for its hospitality during the completion of
this article. The first author would also like to express his gratitude to the Simons Foundation and the Fondation Sciences Mathématiques de Paris for their partial financial support
of this research.</p>
</div>
